Melee Weapon Attack: [[/r 1d20+14]]{+14} to hit, reach 10 ft., one target. Hit: 22 ([[/damage 3d8 + 9 type=piercing]]) damage. If the target is a Large or smaller creature, it must succeed on a [[/save ability=dex dc=19]] saving throw or be swallowed by the eyestalk. A swallowed creature is &Reference[condition=blinded] and &Reference[condition=restrained], it has &Reference[rule=totalcover]{total cover} against attacks and other effects outside the eyestalk, and it takes 21 ([[/damage 6d6 type=acid]]) damage at the start of each of the eyestalk's turns.

If the eyestalk takes 30 damage or more on a single turn from a creature inside it, the eyestalk must succeed on a [[/save ability=con dc=21]] saving throw at the end of that turn or regurgitate all swallowed creatures, which fall &Reference[condition=prone] in a space within 10 feet of the eyestalk. If the eyestalk dies, a swallowed creature is no longer &Reference[condition=restrained] by it and can escape from the corpse by using 20 feet of movement, exiting &Reference[condition=prone].

The eyestalk creates an area of magical devastation in a 150-foot cone. Any creature in that area must succeed on a [[/save ability=dex dc=16]] saving throw or take 55 ([[/damage 10d10 type=necrotic]]) damage. If this damage reduces a creature to 0 hit points, its body becomes a pile of fine violet dust.
The eyestalk can burrow through solid rock at half its burrow speed and leaves a 10-foot-diameter tunnel in its wake.

biography.value:
Fawful — The Assistant Who Became the Architect

Fawful is the most dangerous individual currently operating in the Mushroom Kingdom's sphere of influence who is not a god, a dimensional anomaly, or a force of nature. He is a small Beanish man with enormous glasses, speech patterns that weaponize grammar into incomprehensibility, and a mind that processes strategic complexity the way other minds process breathing—automatically, constantly, without conscious effort, producing results that make brilliant analysts feel stupid and careful planners feel careless.

He started as an assistant. This is the detail that every analyst who studies Fawful returns to with mounting horror, because the things Fawful has accomplished since ceasing to be someone else's assistant suggest capabilities that were always present but previously constrained by service to a lesser intellect. Cackletta, the witch he served during the Beanbean Kingdom Crisis of 1012 BF, was powerful. Fawful was something else entirely. Cackletta wanted a voice. Fawful wanted everything.

When Mario and Luigi defeated Cackletta in the Beanbean Kingdom, Fawful escaped. He disappeared from records for twenty-eight years. Official histories assumed he was dead, irrelevant, a footnote in a crisis that had been resolved. This assumption was incorrect in ways that are now horrifyingly apparent.

During those twenty-eight years, Fawful was building. Not visibly—there were no armies, no territories, no declarations of intent. He was building QUIETLY, assembling a network of alliances, resources, and capabilities that nobody detected until it was too late to prevent. He built relationships with dragons—not one dragon, not two, but five confirmed alliances with creatures whose individual power exceeds conventional military formations. He established himself in Mushroom Kingdom territory by taking advantage of the civil war's chaos, occupying positions that nobody else wanted because nobody else saw their strategic value. He planted agents in every faction, cultivated intelligence sources that span the political spectrum, and developed technology that combines Beanish ingenuity with sources of power that legitimate engineers won't touch.

By the time the current crisis began, Fawful had been the most powerful non-state actor in the region for at least a decade, and nobody knew. He revealed himself on Highsun 10, 1040 BF, by hosting a victory gala—a social event attended by scouts from multiple factions, during which Fawful casually announced his dragon alliances and demonstrated a level of organizational capability that intelligence services across the kingdom had completely failed to detect. The gala served multiple purposes: it established Fawful as a power to be negotiated with rather than dismissed; it provided cover for intelligence operations by Embercap and Mistveil (during which Chief Thornpaw's revelation about Peach's secret hatch was extracted); and it announced to everyone paying attention that the civil war's factional landscape had just acquired a new, major player who had been preparing for this moment for nearly three decades.

Fawful currently controls Peach's Castle—the symbolic and strategic heart of the Mushroom Kingdom, occupied through mechanisms that suggest either overwhelming force or infiltration so complete that resistance was irrelevant by the time his occupation became visible. His garrison is estimated at over five hundred personnel, supplemented by mechanical constructs of his own design, supported by dragon allies whose individual combat capability exceeds what most military formations can counter. Operation HOMECOMING—Mistveil's infiltration to locate the secret hatch—operates inside this fortress, with four operatives embedded in Fawful's servant staff, surrounded by forces that could destroy them instantly if their cover was compromised.

Understanding Fawful requires understanding that his apparent chaos is performance. The speech patterns—"I HAVE FURY!" and the elaborate food metaphors and the grammar that seems to have been assembled by someone who learned language from a malfunctioning dictionary—are deliberate. They make him seem unhinged. They make opponents underestimate his intelligence. They create cognitive dissonance between what Fawful says and what Fawful does, forcing anyone interacting with him to choose between taking his words seriously (which makes them seem foolish when the words are nonsensical) and dismissing his words (which makes them miss genuine intelligence buried in the metaphors).

Fawful is not unhinged. Fawful is the most rationally calculating entity in the current crisis who also happens to express himself like a caffeinated thesaurus having a breakdown. The calculations are perfect. The expression is theater. And the theater serves the calculations, because nobody prepares adequate defenses against someone they've decided is a clown.

His grudge against the Mario Brothers—specifically against Luigi, "the green mustache"—has survived twenty-eight years without diminishing. Fawful remembers. Fawful always remembers. The defeat in the Beanbean Kingdom wasn't merely a setback; it was a humiliation that Fawful has been processing through the specific lens of someone whose entire self-worth was tied to serving Cackletta competently and who failed to prevent her defeat. That failure created a wound that three decades of empire-building haven't healed. It may have created the MOTIVATION for the empire-building—the need to prove that Fawful is not a failed assistant but a force in his own right, capable of accomplishments that dwarf anything Cackletta imagined.

What Fawful is planning—beyond the occupation, beyond the alliances, beyond the gala announcement—connects to something he calls "the completion" in fragmentary references recovered from Bramblehaven's intelligence cache. The completion is expected before the end of the current month. Its nature is unknown. Its scope, based on the resources Fawful has assembled, is terrifying. Five dragons. Hundreds of soldiers. Peach's Castle. Twenty-eight years of preparation.

Whatever the completion is, it's not simple conquest. Fawful could have conquered territory overtly at any point during his preparation period. He chose not to. He waited. He built. He positioned. And now, with dimensional instability fracturing reality around Raventree Manor and the kingdom's factions tearing each other apart, he's ready to complete whatever he's been building toward since a green mustache helped defeat his mistress in the Beanbean Kingdom twenty-eight years ago.
biography.public: A small Beanish man with enormous round glasses and a grin that contains too many teeth arranged in configurations that shouldn't fit a mouth that size. He hovers in a mechanical pod of his own design and speaks in metaphors that make linguists weep. Everything about him says 'harmless lunatic' except his eyes, which say 'I've been planning this since before you were born.'

description.value:
Fawful's signature mechanical headgear serves as transportation, weapons platform, and personal protection system. The device sits atop his head like a helmet and extends into a hovering pod that allows sustained flight and provides a stable platform for his various weapon systems. The engineering is Beanish in origin—a tradition that prioritizes function over aesthetics and considers exposed wiring a design feature rather than a flaw—but the power source is something Fawful added himself during his twenty-eight years of independent development.

The headgear contains a miniaturized power core that Fawful claims runs on "the mustard of your doom," which—after extensive analysis by multiple intelligence services—appears to mean concentrated fury channeled through alchemical compounds that shouldn't be stable and yet somehow are. The core powers the flight mechanism, the weapons systems, the shields, and the various secondary functions that Fawful has added over decades of continuous modification. The headgear is never the same twice; he improves it constantly, adding capabilities and refining systems with an obsessive attention to detail that suggests the device is as much a part of his identity as the glasses and the grin.

The headgear provides AC 18 (natural armor), flight at 50 feet with hover capability, and serves as the delivery system for Fawful's various attack options. Destroying the headgear (AC 18, 50 HP, immune to psychic and poison damage) grounds Fawful and removes his access to most ranged weaponry, but he remains dangerous even without it—the headgear supplements his capabilities rather than creating them.
description.chat: The headgear hums with energy that shouldn't exist in a device this size, carrying its pilot through the air with the casual defiance of someone who considers physics a suggestion.

unidentified.name: Mechanical Hover Platform
unidentified.description: A complex mechanical device worn as headgear that provides flight and serves as a weapons platform. The engineering is unlike any recognized tradition, and the power source defies standard analysis.

description.value:
The headgear's primary weapon system: a concentrated beam of energy that Fawful fires from apertures mounted on either side of the pod. The beam's color shifts based on Fawful's emotional state—red when angry, green when amused, purple when he's about to do something that will make everyone present wish they'd stayed home. The damage type varies correspondingly: fire when red, acid when green, necrotic when purple. Fawful controls the beam's emotional calibration instinctively, weaponizing his own psychological state with an efficiency that trained magical artificers find both impressive and deeply unsettling.

The beam fires in a 60-foot line that is 5 feet wide. Each creature in the line must make a DC 19 Dexterity saving throw, taking 8d6 damage on a failure (type depending on emotional state) or half on a success. Fawful can fire the beam twice per round, alternating between apertures, and the rapid-fire capability means enemies who dodge the first beam often move into the path of the second.
description.chat: "I HAVE FURY!" The beam confirms this assessment, delivering concentrated emotional energy in wavelengths that burn, dissolve, or decay depending on which emotion is doing the burning.

unidentified.name: Variable Energy Beam
unidentified.description: A beam weapon that changes damage type based on the wielder's emotional state. The variability makes defensive preparation difficult.

description.value:
The headgear contains a powerful vacuum system that Fawful can activate to inhale objects, projectiles, and even small creatures toward himself. The vacuum creates a 30-foot cone of pulling force that requires each creature in the area to succeed on a DC 17 Strength saving throw or be pulled 15 feet toward Fawful. Objects not being held are automatically pulled to Fawful's position. Projectiles fired through the cone have disadvantage on attack rolls as the vacuum disrupts their trajectory.

Fawful uses the vacuum tactically: pulling melee combatants toward his ranged position to create confusion, absorbing thrown weapons and repurposing them, and—in one documented instance—inhaling a cloud of smoke that an enemy was using for concealment and spitting it back as a choking hazard. The vacuum's versatility reflects Fawful's general approach to engineering: build something that does one thing and then find seventy-three additional applications through creativity that borders on mania.
description.chat: The headgear inhales and suddenly everything not nailed down starts moving toward the small man with the enormous grin, including you.

description.value:
During his twenty-eight years of preparation, Fawful obtained and consumed a fragment of the Dark Star—an artifact of catastrophic power that nearly destroyed the Mushroom Kingdom during a crisis that official records have minimized even more aggressively than they minimized the Chaos Heart Crisis. The Dark Star is the counterpart to the Star Rod and the Star Spirits: where they represent hope, wishes, and cosmic benevolence, the Dark Star represents entropy, corruption, and the consumption of light.

Consuming the fragment didn't grant Fawful cosmic power on the scale of the God Toad or even a Star Shard Bearer. What it did was fundamentally alter his physiology, granting him resistances and capabilities that Beanish biology doesn't normally support: resistance to fire, lightning, and cold damage; immunity to charmed and frightened conditions; and the ability to generate the fury energy that powers his headgear from his own body rather than from external fuel sources. He is his own power plant. The dark fragment makes him self-sustaining in ways that conventional technology cannot match.

The fragment also connects him to the broader cosmic architecture that the God Toad's scattered Star Shards represent. The Dark Star fragment is not one of the nine Shards, but it resonates with them—a discordant note in the cosmic music that the Shards collectively produce. Fawful can sense Star Shard activity at distances that suggest cosmic awareness operating through the dark fragment's connection to the star-power spectrum. He knows about the Oracle. He knows about Bryan. He may know about the God Toad's grand design, though his interpretation of that design would reflect the dark fragment's corrupted perspective.
description.chat: Something dark powers him from within, consumed decades ago, integrated so thoroughly that the distinction between Fawful and the fragment has become academic.

description.value: Fawful makes three attacks: two Fury Beam blasts and one of the following: Vacuum Inhale, Fawful Bomb deployment, or Dark Pulse. He typically opens with Vacuum Inhale to disrupt enemy formations, follows with Fury Beams to deal damage to clustered targets, and reserves Dark Pulse for situations where enemies are resistant to his beam weapons.
description.chat: Three attacks from different systems, each one calculated to complement the others in a sequence that looks chaotic and functions with mechanical precision.

description.value:
Small mechanical devices that Fawful deploys from compartments in his headgear, each one shaped like a miniature version of his own face—grinning, bespectacled, and entirely too cheerful for something that explodes. The bombs hover briefly after deployment, tracking toward designated targets with rudimentary guidance systems before detonating in bursts of fury energy.

Each bomb targets a creature within 60 feet. The target must make a DC 17 Dexterity saving throw, taking 4d8 fire damage on a failure or half on a success. Fawful can deploy up to three bombs as a single action, targeting the same or different creatures. The bombs can be destroyed before detonation (AC 12, 5 HP each), but their small size and erratic flight patterns impose disadvantage on attack rolls made to hit them.

The grinning faces are Fawful's personal aesthetic choice. He considers them intimidating. Everyone else considers them deeply creepy in a way that intimidation doesn't quite capture.
description.chat: Miniature grinning faces hover toward their targets with the cheerful inevitability of something that's about to ruin someone's day.

unidentified.name: Guided Explosive Devices
unidentified.description: Small hovering bombs shaped like faces that track toward targets before detonating. The design aesthetic is deeply unsettling.

description.value:
Fawful channels the Dark Star fragment within him, releasing a pulse of concentrated entropic energy in a 30-foot radius centered on himself. Each creature in the area must make a DC 19 Constitution saving throw. On a failure, a creature takes 6d10 necrotic damage and has its hit point maximum reduced by an amount equal to the necrotic damage taken until it finishes a long rest. On a success, a creature takes half damage and suffers no maximum reduction.

The Dark Pulse is Fawful's most powerful single attack, and he uses it sparingly—the fragment's energy is finite and regenerates slowly, meaning overuse could deplete reserves he needs for the completion. When he does use it, the effect is unmistakable: the area around Fawful dims as light itself is consumed by the pulse, colors bleach to grayscale, and living things feel a moment of absolute despair as the dark energy passes through them.

The pulse also disrupts magical effects in the area. Active spells of 3rd level or lower in the area are automatically dispelled. Higher-level spells require a DC 19 check using Fawful's Intelligence modifier to dispel. This disruption reflects the Dark Star's fundamental nature: it doesn't just damage, it UNMAKES, reducing complex magical constructs to their component energies.
description.chat: Light dies around him. Color bleaches. Hope folds. The dark fragment speaks through Fawful's body and everything within range learns what entropy feels like from the inside.

description.value:
Fawful speaks in elaborately mangled metaphors, food-based analogies, and grammatical constructions that seem to have been assembled by someone who learned language from a book about language that was itself badly translated. "I HAVE FURY!" "Your power is the power of a baby ant who cannot lift even the smallest grain of mustard!" "The taste of your defeat will be like the sourness of a lemon that has married the bitterness of a thousand coffees!"

This is deliberate. The speech patterns are a tactical tool that creates cognitive dissonance in opponents: they can't take him seriously because his words are absurd, but they can't dismiss him because his actions are devastatingly effective. The gap between how Fawful sounds and what Fawful does creates a processing delay that gives him tactical advantage—enemies who are trying to parse his metaphors are not preparing for his attacks.

Creatures who hear Fawful speak for the first time must succeed on a DC 14 Wisdom saving throw or be momentarily confused by the dissonance, suffering disadvantage on their first attack roll or ability check against him as their minds struggle to reconcile "food metaphor lunatic" with "extremely dangerous combatant." Creatures who have previously encountered Fawful are immune to this effect, having learned the hard way that the mustard is always metaphorical and the fury is always real.
description.chat: "You are like a sandwich that has forgotten its bread, which is to say you are merely the MEAT and I am the TEETH!" He is already attacking while you try to figure out what that means.

description.value:
Fawful maintains confirmed alliances with five dragons, each one representing military capability that exceeds conventional military formations. The dragons are bound to Fawful through arrangements that intelligence services have been unable to fully characterize—some appear to involve mutual benefit, others suggest leverage or coercion, and at least one appears to involve the kind of genuine respect that powerful beings occasionally develop for minds they consider equals.

In combat encounters, Fawful can use a legendary action (2 actions) to call for dragon support if a dragon ally is within 1 mile. The dragon arrives within 1d4 rounds and acts on its own initiative, following Fawful's general tactical direction without requiring turn-by-turn commands. The dragon alliance transforms any encounter with Fawful from a fight against a single powerful individual into a fight against that individual plus a creature whose breath weapon alone might be sufficient to end the engagement.

The relationship between Fawful and the Dragon Conspiracy—the fabricated war between dragons and the Regal Empire maintained through sonic control devices—is unclear. Fawful may be aware of the conspiracy and exploiting it. He may have allies among the "free" dragons who have escaped sonic control. Or he may be using the conspiracy's infrastructure for his own purposes, piggybacking on Legion technology with modifications the Legion doesn't know about.
description.chat: Five dragons answer when he calls. Five. The number matters because one dragon is a crisis and five dragons is an army.

description.value: Three times per day, when Fawful fails a saving throw, he can choose to succeed instead. The Dark Star fragment's energy reinforces his existence against magical effects that would incapacitate or control him. He has survived things that should have killed him—Cackletta's defeat, decades of underground operation, the consumption of a cosmic fragment that should have destroyed his physiology—and simple magical compulsion isn't going to stop someone who has been too stubborn to die for twenty-eight years.
description.chat: The spell fails. Fawful grins. "Your magic is like a sandwich thrown at a WALL. It makes a mess but the wall does not CARE."

description.value:
Fawful can take 3 legendary actions, choosing from the options below. Only one legendary action can be used at a time and only at the end of another creature's turn.

Reposition (1 action): Fawful moves up to his fly speed without provoking opportunity attacks, repositioning to optimal range for his weapons.

Bomb Drop (1 action): Fawful deploys a single Fawful Bomb at a target within 60 feet.

Dragon Call (2 actions): Fawful signals a dragon ally within 1 mile. The dragon arrives within 1d4 rounds.

Fury Overcharge (3 actions): Fawful overcharges his headgear, firing a supercharged Fury Beam that deals double damage (16d6) in a 60-foot line. After using this ability, the headgear requires 1 round to cool down, during which Fawful cannot use Fury Beam or Fawful Bombs.
description.chat: Between other people's turns, Fawful repositions, deploys, and overcharges, operating at a tempo that conventional combatants cannot match.

description.value:
Fawful remembers the "green mustache." Twenty-eight years have not diminished the grudge against Luigi that was born when the Mario Brothers defeated Cackletta in the Beanbean Kingdom. This grudge is not rational—or rather, it is rational within Fawful's internal logic, where his worth was defined by service to Cackletta and his failure to prevent her defeat invalidated that worth entirely. Luigi represents the moment Fawful became nothing. Everything since—the empire-building, the dragon alliances, the Dark Star fragment, the occupation of Peach's Castle—has been partly motivated by the need to prove that the nothing can become everything.

When Fawful encounters Luigi (or anyone associated with the Mario Brothers), he gains advantage on all attack rolls against that target for 1 round as fury-fueled focus sharpen his capabilities. However, he also has disadvantage on Wisdom saving throws for the same duration, as the emotional intensity that enhances his combat performance also makes him more vulnerable to effects that target his clearly compromised judgment regarding anything green-mustache-related.

This vulnerability is exploitable. Anyone who recognizes Fawful's grudge can provoke it deliberately, trading increased danger from his enhanced attacks for the tactical opportunity created by his weakened mental defenses. Making Fawful angry makes him dangerous. Making Fawful angry about Luigi makes him dangerous AND predictable, and predictability in combat is a weakness that skilled opponents know how to exploit.
description.chat: "The green mustache. I REMEMBER the green mustache. I have been remembering for TWENTY-EIGHT YEARS." The fury isn't metaphorical anymore.

description.value:
Fawful is working toward something he calls "the completion," referenced in fragmentary intelligence recovered from Bramblehaven and in overheard conversations at his gala. The completion is expected before the end of the current month. Its nature is unknown to outside observers. Its scope, based on the resources Fawful has assembled—five dragons, hundreds of soldiers, Peach's Castle, the Dark Star fragment, twenty-eight years of preparation—suggests an event of transformative significance.

The completion may involve the dimensional instability at Raventree Manor. The completion may involve the Star Shards and the God Toad's grand design. The completion may involve Peach's secret hatch and whatever evidence it contains. The completion may involve something entirely separate that nobody has anticipated because Fawful has been planning in dimensions that conventional analysis doesn't reach.

Whatever it is, the completion represents the culmination of twenty-eight years of work by the most strategically gifted mind currently operating in the region. It will not be simple. It will not be preventable through conventional means. And it will not be what anyone expects, because Fawful's genius lies precisely in doing things that nobody expects while making everyone believe he's doing something else entirely.
description.chat: "The completion is like a CAKE that has been BAKING for twenty-eight YEARS and now the OVEN is opening and YOU are not READY for how delicious the FURY will TASTE." He means it. All of it. Including the cake part, somehow.

description.value:
Fawful has been preparing for the current moment for twenty-eight years. This preparation manifests as comprehensive contingency planning that covers virtually every scenario. He has agents in every major faction. He has supply caches in locations that other powers don't know exist. He has escape routes from every position he occupies. He has backup plans for his backup plans, each one designed for a specific failure mode that his analysis identified as possible.

Mechanically, Fawful cannot be surprised. He has advantage on saving throws against traps and ambushes. Once per day, when an enemy action would produce a result that Fawful didn't anticipate, the DM may rule that Fawful DID anticipate it—he had a contingency in place, a prepared response, a resource positioned exactly where it needed to be. This reflects not supernatural prescience but the kind of exhaustive strategic preparation that twenty-eight years of obsessive planning produces.

The limitation is that Fawful's preparations are based on his own analysis, which is brilliant but not omniscient. Truly random events—the kind of chaos that the party generates through unpredictable decision-making and the involvement of entities like Waluigi—can exceed his contingency framework. He can plan for competent enemies. He cannot plan for incomprehensible ones.
description.chat: He planned for this. Whatever this is, he planned for it twenty-eight years ago and has been refining the plan ever since. You are not surprising him. You are confirming his expectations.

reasons: Long-range weapon with no melee option → sniper

The Usurper at Bowser's Gate — Fawthful's Forces

Status: Historical actor — identified in the 18 Harvestide, 1035 BF Bowser Castle filings; current whereabouts not established

The historical record identifies Fawthful as the commander who turned a compromised Bowser's Castle into an invasion route. With Mimbus, Cackletta, a dragon, Magikoopas, and defecting Koopa troops in the field, Fawthful treated the throne as a temporary obstacle on the way to ruling the world—or being worshipped by it.

Evidence

  • Headgear Ray — “Unknown — hostile commander”
  • Extra Attack — “Unknown — hostile commander”
  • Compromised Access — “The historical record identifies Fawthful as the commander who turned a compromised Bowser's Castle into an invasion route.”
  • Moving Terror Weapon — “The operation began with compromised access, used a dragon as a moving terror weapon, and turned the castle's own garrison into a question Bowser could not answer quickly enough.”
  • Not Resolved as Fawful — “The archive keeps Fawthful distinct from the older Fawful record because the assault account uses this name and does not resolve whether it is a new identity, a title, or a deliberate distortion.”

The commander who turned a compromised castle into an invasion route and then stated the plan at the gate: 'When people come to the castle, they will see me as the king. I will be this world's god.' Asked why a bean wanted Bowser's castle: 'Power. I control the capital. You do not. I control the big Bowser Castle. You do not. Simple.'

He fights from a hoverpad above the broken floor with the vacuum apparatus on his head. He sucked Cackletta into it when she became a dangerous guest; she is still in there when this session opens, and she comes out when he decides, or when he is losing. He threatened to suck Bowser up too. He cannot — Bowser is Large — but the sheet lets him try, and lets him say so.

The archive keeps Fawthful distinct from the older Fawful record (fawful); do not resolve that at the table. The present-day article is fawthful. Legendary Resistances are two because the record shows him surviving a throne-room full of fire by not being where it landed.

From the record: the hoverpad, the vacuum apparatus, the claim at the gate; he told the dragon there would be consequences.

description.value: Ranged spell attack, 120 feet. Green light with a headache in it.
Fawthful makes two Fury Ray attacks, or one Fury Ray and uses Inhale if it is available.

A 30-foot cone from the helmet's intake. Each creature in the cone makes a DC 16 Strength saving throw. A Medium or smaller creature that fails is pulled 20 feet toward Fawthful, and if it ends within 5 feet of him it is swallowed into the apparatus. A Large creature that fails is pulled 10 feet and cannot be swallowed, whatever Fawthful says. A swallowed creature is blinded and restrained, has total cover against everything outside, and takes 2d6 bludgeoning damage at the start of each of its turns. It can escape with a DC 16 Strength (Athletics) check as an action, or by spinning in its shell (Shell Vault); a swallowed creature that deals 15 or more damage to the inside in a single turn pops the seal, and everything in there comes out in a 15-foot line.

Fawthful ejects Cackletta — or any other swallowed creature — into an unoccupied space within 15 feet. Cackletta arrives at full hit points and furious, and acts on Fawthful's initiative count minus 10. He does this the first time he is below half his hit points, or earlier if the room bores him.

One creature within 60 feet that can hear Fawthful makes a DC 16 Wisdom saving throw. On a failure it has disadvantage on attack rolls against anyone but Fawthful until the end of its next turn. Bowser saves at disadvantage; the record is clear that he finds the bean genuinely infuriating.

When an ally within 60 feet misses an attack or fails a check, Fawthful screams about consequences. The ally takes 1d8 psychic damage and has advantage on its next attack roll before the end of its next turn. The dragon has heard this already.

Fly 40 (hover), five feet above whatever is left of the floor. A ground pound or Stomp within 10 feet of him forces a DC 15 Dexterity saving throw; on a failure he is knocked off the pad, lands prone, and cannot fly until he spends a bonus action remounting it.

Fawthful claims half the castle was infiltrated before the dragon arrived, and the garrison sheet agrees. Red-Armband Koopas and Chain-Puller Goombas within 60 feet of him open doors and portcullises as a bonus action instead of an action.
If Fawthful fails a saving throw, he can choose to succeed instead.

Fawthful can take 2 legendary actions, choosing from the options below, only at the end of another creature's turn, regaining them at the start of his turn.

  • Fury Ray. One Fury Ray attack.
  • Hover Dash. He moves up to 20 feet without provoking opportunity attacks.
  • Cackle (Costs 2 Actions). Mustard Monologue against up to three creatures.

A small Fawthful drone appeared in the next room while the surviving force argued over an empty train track. The group had sent someone to tell Bowser they had survived the dragon; the messenger had not returned, and the drone had. One Goomba walked toward it, and the fight began there.

A machine that waits for somebody to come close enough to attack. What it sees, Fawthful sees; what it finds, Fawthful's next patrol finds a few rounds later. Kill it before it finishes looking.

From the record: the drone in the next room at Toad Town Station.

description.value: Ranged, 30/60. Two copper prongs and a spark.
A drone that has not moved is a machine in a corner: a DC 15 Wisdom (Perception) check to notice. It has advantage on initiative and on its first attack roll of the fight.
Fawthful sees what the drone sees. When a drone spots the surviving force, or Bowser, the next hostile patrol arrives 1d4 rounds later. Destroying it within a round of being spotted sends nothing.
It plays a recording of Fawthful laughing: Mustard Monologue against one creature within 30 feet, DC 11.
When reduced to 0 hit points the drone bursts: each creature within 5 feet makes a DC 12 Dexterity saving throw, taking 2d6 lightning damage on a failure or half as much on a success.

details.appearance: A one-armed Toad with a colorful Feywild aura, a scar from the Estragon Island escape, and a third multi-dimensional sensory eye. The missing arm is permanent in the current record; no prosthetic is assumed.
details.trait: I apologize to the room first. Then I test the window—with the arm I have.
details.ideal: Continuity and protection. The planes may disagree about which Dan I am, but I decide who I protect.
details.bond: The party that keeps finding me across mazes, estates, and collapsing realities, and the people who cannot survive without a shield in the doorway.
details.flaw: I trust the nearest exit more than the person explaining why it is locked, and I hate being treated as fragile.
details.eyes: Two ordinary eyes and one Feyward sensory eye
details.faith: Unresolved; has encountered forces that call themselves gods
details.skin: Toad green with Feywild color shift

languages.custom: Can recognize Feyward planar terminology; speaks under pressure with uncertain confidence.

armorProf.custom: Light, medium, and heavy armor;shields. Dan fights one-handed and does not receive a second-weapon benefit.

weaponProf.custom: Simple and martial weapons;longsword;one-handed use only.

description.value: Dan survived Prismari's school, a goblin ambush, the Mazebound, and multiple plane fractures. Suggested proficiencies: Insight, Persuasion, Survival, and Sylvan.

Once per short rest, open the third eye for 1 minute. You can perceive invisible creatures and identify the approximate seam of a nearby portal or planar disguise. The eye is noticeable and may attract attention.

Dan is proficient with windows, thornbushes, locked rooms, and routes that were not designed as exits. Once per short rest, gain advantage on one check made to escape a confined or unfamiliar location.
Dan can recognize that his memories do not line up with another Dan. He has advantage on checks to notice identity substitution, but disadvantage when asked to prove which history is original.
A colorful aura surrounds Dan. It is visible to trained Fey creatures and may identify him as a dimensional contaminant, visitor, or valuable specimen.
Dan may reroll one failed attack or escape check per long rest, but the reroll must be described as a second attempt, not effortless competence.
Dan knows the maze took him once. He has advantage on one check per journey to notice when a route is looping, singing, or trying to remove him from the party.

Wondrous item, rare (requires attunement by a cleric or paladin of good alignment)

This platinum amulet is shaped like the sun with a large crystal set in its center. It is sacred to the good-hearted faithful of Barovia and predates any organized church there. Legend says a giant raven (or an angel in raven form) delivered it to the paladin Lugdana, who used it against vampires until her death.

The holy symbol has a number of charges equal to your proficiency bonus + 2 (minimum 3). It regains all expended charges daily at dawn.

While you are attuned to the holy symbol, it functions as a holy symbol for the purpose of spellcasting and channel divinity.

Base Powers (Character Level 3–4)

  • Hold Lesser Vampires (1 charge). As an action, present the holy symbol. Vampire spawn within 15 feet of you must succeed on a Wisdom saving throw (DC = 8 + your proficiency bonus + your Wisdom or Charisma modifier, whichever is higher) or be paralyzed for 1 minute. A paralyzed target can repeat the saving throw at the end of each of its turns, ending the effect on itself on a success. True vampires are immune to this effect.

  • Empowered Turning (2 charges). When you use Turn Undead or Turn the Unholy, you may expend 2 charges. Undead of CR 1 or lower have disadvantage on the saving throw against the effect.

Level 5–8 Improvements

  • Charge maximum becomes proficiency bonus + 3.

  • Hold Lesser Vampires range increases to 20 feet and now also affects vampires of CR 5 or lower (still no effect on Strahd or unique named vampires of higher CR unless the DM rules otherwise).

  • Empowered Turning cost drops to 1 charge and affects undead of CR 2 or lower.

  • Sunlight (3 charges). As an action, present the holy symbol to shed bright light in a 15-foot radius and dim light for an additional 15 feet. The light is sunlight and lasts for 1 minute or until you dismiss it (no action required).

Level 9–12 Improvements

  • Charge maximum becomes proficiency bonus + 4.

  • Hold Vampires (1 charge). Range increases to 30 feet. Affects all vampires and vampire spawn (except those the DM designates as legendary or uniquely resistant). Paralyzed duration remains 1 minute with saves at the end of each turn.

  • Empowered Turning now affects undead of CR 3 or lower and costs 1 charge.

  • Sunlight radius increases to 20 feet bright / 20 feet dim and lasts 5 minutes.

Level 13+ (Full Power)

  • Charge maximum becomes proficiency bonus + 5 (capped at 10).

  • Hold Vampires uses the original DC 15 (or your spell save DC if higher) and functions exactly as the classic version.

  • Empowered Turning costs 2 charges and grants disadvantage to all undead against your Turn Undead / Turn the Unholy.

  • Sunlight (4 charges) sheds bright light in a 30-foot radius and dim light for an additional 30 feet for up to 10 minutes.

Additional Notes

  • The item never exceeds 10 charges regardless of proficiency bonus.

  • At every stage the light created by the Sunlight property is true sunlight for the purpose of vampire weaknesses and similar effects.

  • The DM can further gate specific powers (especially affecting true vampires or Strahd himself) behind story milestones if desired.

Michael Broussard

Paladins are united by their oaths to stand against the forces of annihilation and corruption. Whether sworn before a god's altar, in a sacred glade before nature spirits, or in a moment of desperation and grief with the dead as the only witnesses, a Paladin's oath is a powerful bond. It is a source of power that turns a devout warrior into a blessed champion.

Paladins train to learn the skills of combat, mastering a variety of weapons and armor. Even so, their martial skills are secondary to the magical power they wield: power to heal the injured, smite their foes, and protect the helpless and those who fight at their side.

Almost by definition, the life of a Paladin is an adventuring life, for every Paladin lives on the front lines of the cosmic struggle against annihilation. Fighters are rare enough among the ranks of a world's armies, but even fewer people can claim the calling of a Paladin. When they do receive the call, these blessed folk turn from their former occupations and take up arms and magic.

Level 1: Lay on Hands

Your blessed touch can heal wounds. You have a pool of healing power that replenishes when you finish a @variantrule[Long Rest|XPHB]. With that pool, you can restore a total number of @variantrule[Hit Points|XPHB] equal to five times your Paladin level.

As a @variantrule[Bonus Action|XPHB], you can touch a creature (which could be yourself) and draw power from the pool of healing to restore a number of @variantrule[Hit Points|XPHB] to that creature, up to the maximum amount remaining in the pool.

You can also expend 5 @variantrule[Hit Points|XPHB] from the pool of healing power to remove the &Reference[condition=Poisoned] condition from the creature; those points don't also restore @variantrule[Hit Points|XPHB] to the creature.

Level 1: Spellcasting

You have learned to cast spells through prayer and meditation. See chapter 7 for the rules on spellcasting. The information below details how you use those rules with Paladin spells, which appear in the Paladin spell list later in the class's description.

Spell Slots. The Paladin Features table shows how many spell slots you have to cast your level 1+ spells. You regain all expended slots when you finish a @variantrule[Long Rest|XPHB].

Prepared Spells of Level 1+. You prepare the list of level 1+ spells that are available for you to cast with this feature. To start, choose two level 1 Paladin spells. @spell[Heroism|XPHB] and @spell[Searing Smite|XPHB] are recommended.

The number of spells on your list increases as you gain Paladin levels, as shown in the Prepared Spells column of the Paladin Features table. Whenever that number increases, choose additional Paladin spells until the number of spells on your list matches the number in the Paladin Features table. The chosen spells must be of a level for which you have spell slots. For example, if you're a level 5 Paladin, your list of prepared spells can include six Paladin spells of level 1 or 2 in any combination.

If another Paladin feature gives you spells that you always have prepared, those spells don't count against the number of spells you can prepare with this feature, but those spells otherwise count as Paladin spells for you.

Changing Your Prepared Spells. Whenever you finish a @variantrule[Long Rest|XPHB], you can replace one spell on your list with another Paladin spell for which you have spell slots.

Spellcasting Ability. Charisma is your spellcasting ability for your Paladin spells.

Spellcasting Focus. You can use a @item[Holy Symbol|XPHB] as a @variantrule[Spellcasting Focus|XPHB] for your Paladin spells.

Level 1: Weapon Mastery

Your training with weapons allows you to use the @variantrule[weapon mastery properties|XPHB|mastery properties] of two kinds of weapons of your choice with which you have proficiency, such as @item[Longsword|XPHB|Longswords] and @item[Javelin|XPHB|Javelins].

Whenever you finish a @variantrule[Long Rest|XPHB], you can change the kinds of weapons you chose. For example, you could switch to using the @variantrule[weapon mastery properties|XPHB|mastery properties] of @item[Halberd|XPHB|Halberds] and @item[Flail|XPHB|Flails].

Level 2: Fighting Style

You gain a Fighting Style feat of your choice. Instead of choosing one of those feats, you can choose the option below.

Blessed Warrior. You learn two Cleric cantrips of your choice. @spell[Guidance|XPHB] and @spell[Sacred Flame|XPHB] are recommended. The chosen cantrips count as Paladin spells for you, and Charisma is your spellcasting ability for them. Whenever you gain a Paladin level, you can replace one of these cantrips with another Cleric cantrip.

Level 2: Paladin's Smite

You always have the @spell[Divine Smite|XPHB] spell prepared. In addition, you can cast it without expending a spell slot, but you must finish a @variantrule[Long Rest|XPHB] before you can cast it in this way again.

Level 3: Channel Divinity

You can channel divine energy directly from the Outer Planes, using it to fuel magical effects. You start with one such effect: Divine Sense, which is described below. Other Paladin features give additional Channel Divinity effect options. Each time you use this class's Channel Divinity, you choose which effect from this class to create.

You can use this class's Channel Divinity twice. You regain one of its expended uses when you finish a @variantrule[Short Rest|XPHB], and you regain all expended uses when you finish a @variantrule[Long Rest|XPHB]. You gain an additional use when you reach Paladin level 11.

If a Channel Divinity effect requires a saving throw, the DC equals the spell save DC from this class's Spellcasting feature.

Divine Sense. As a @variantrule[Bonus Action|XPHB], you can open your awareness to detect Celestials, Fiends, and Undead. For the next 10 minutes or until you have the &Reference[condition=Incapacitated] condition, you know the location of any creature of those types within 60 feet of yourself, and you know its creature type. Within the same radius, you also detect the presence of any place or object that has been consecrated or desecrated, as with the @spell[Hallow|XPHB] spell.

Level 3: Paladin Subclass

You gain a Paladin subclass of your choice. A subclass is a specialization that grants you features at certain Paladin levels. For the rest of your career, you gain each of your subclass's features that are of your Paladin level or lower.

Breaking Your Oath

A Paladin tries to hold to the highest standards of conduct, but even the most dedicated are fallible. Sometimes a Paladin transgresses their oath.

A Paladin who has broken a vow typically seeks absolution, spending an all-night vigil as a sign of penitence or undertaking a fast. After a rite of forgiveness, the Paladin starts fresh.

If your Paladin unrepentantly violates their oath, talk to your DM. Your Paladin should probably take a more appropriate subclass or even abandon the class and adopt another one.

Level 4: Ability Score Improvement

You gain the @feat[Ability Score Improvement|XPHB] feat or another feat of your choice for which you qualify. You gain this feature again at Paladin levels 8, 12, and 16.

Level 5: Extra Attack

You can attack twice instead of once whenever you take the @action[Attack|XPHB] action on your turn.

Level 5: Faithful Steed

You can call on the aid of an otherworldly steed. You always have the @spell[Find Steed|XPHB] spell prepared.

You can also cast the spell once without expending a spell slot, and you regain the ability to do so when you finish a @variantrule[Long Rest|XPHB].

Level 6: Aura of Protection

You radiate a protective, unseeable aura in a 10-foot @variantrule[Emanation [Area of Effect]|XPHB|Emanation] that originates from you. The aura is inactive while you have the &Reference[condition=Incapacitated] condition.

You and your allies in the aura gain a bonus to saving throws equal to your Charisma modifier (minimum bonus of +1).

If another Paladin is present, a creature can benefit from only one Aura of Protection at a time; the creature chooses which aura while in them.

Level 7: Subclass Feature

You gain a feature from your Paladin Subclass.

Level 8: Ability Score Improvement

You gain the @feat[Ability Score Improvement|XPHB] Feat or another feat of your choice for which you qualify.

Level 9: Abjure Foes

As a @action[Magic|XPHB] action, you can expend one use of this class's Channel Divinity to overwhelm foes with awe. As you present your @item[Holy Symbol|XPHB] or weapon, you can target a number of creatures equal to your Charisma modifier (minimum of one creature) that you can see within 60 feet of yourself. Each target must succeed on a Wisdom saving throw or have the &Reference[condition=Frightened] condition for 1 minute or until it takes any damage. While &Reference[condition=Frightened] in this way, a target can do only one of the following on its turns: move, take an action, or take a @variantrule[Bonus Action|XPHB].

Level 10: Aura of Courage

You and your allies have @variantrule[Immunity|XPHB] to the &Reference[condition=Frightened] condition while in your Aura of Protection. If a &Reference[condition=Frightened] ally enters the aura, that condition has no effect on that ally while there.

Level 11: Radiant Strikes

Your strikes now carry supernatural power. When you hit a target with an attack roll using a Melee weapon or an @variantrule[Unarmed Strike|XPHB], the target takes an extra [[/damage 1d8 type=radiant]] damage.

Level 12: Ability Score Improvement

You gain the @feat[Ability Score Improvement|XPHB] Feat or another feat of your choice for which you qualify.

Level 14: Restoring Touch

When you use Lay On Hands on a creature, you can also remove one or more of the following conditions from the creature: &Reference[condition=Blinded], &Reference[condition=Charmed], &Reference[condition=Deafened], &Reference[condition=Frightened], &Reference[condition=Paralyzed], or &Reference[condition=Stunned]. You must expend 5 @variantrule[Hit Points|XPHB] from the healing pool of Lay On Hands for each of these conditions you remove; those points don't also restore @variantrule[Hit Points|XPHB] to the creature.

Level 15: Subclass Feature

You gain a feature from your Paladin Subclass.

Level 16: Ability Score Improvement

You gain the @feat[Ability Score Improvement|XPHB] Feat or another feat of your choice for which you qualify.

Level 18: Aura Expansion

Your Aura of Protection is now a 30-foot @variantrule[Emanation [Area of Effect]|XPHB|Emanation].

Level 19: Epic Boon

You gain an Epic Boon feat or another feat of your choice for which you qualify. @feat[Boon of Truesight|XPHB] is recommended.

Level 20: Subclass Feature

You gain a feature from your Paladin Subclass.

Oath of the Harvest

The Oath of the Harvest attracts paladins who wish to nourish and heal the world. Often found on aid missions to war-torn lands, such paladins resort to harm only as a means of preventing further suffering. Paladins who swear this oath are more likely than not to heal, feed, and nuture a wounded foe, provided the defeated creature gives its word of honour that it will cease its nefarious activities. They are no fools, however. Typically versed in religion and medicine, these paladins are unlikely to believe the word of creatures inherently inclined to lie, or those that have previously broken their word.

Level 3: Tenets of the Harvest

The tenets of the Oath of the Harvest inspire their followers to seek out potential harm and quell it before it blossoms.

Share Your Meal. Your powers are a gift to be shared; if someone is in need, you must use your power to meet those needs. To eat your fill while another goes hungry is selfish.

Nurture Over Cure. Act in the greatest interest of the many. Find ways to prevent harm before it must be healed.

Permit Prosperity. Whether in matters of love, politics, or war, always give your antagonist the opportunity to change and redeem themselves before casting a fatal judgment. A good meal can serve as the backdrop to such events.

Level 3: Oath Tools

Always keen to fortify others with flavourful food, you've spent hours slicing, dicing, and cooking. You gain proficiency with cook's utensils.

Level 3: Oath Spells

You gain the oath spells at the paladin levels listed in the Oath of the Harvest Spells table See the Sacred Oath class feature for how oath spells work.

Level 3: Channel Divinity: Vow of Sustenance

As a bonus action, you can place a ward around one creature you can see within 60 feet of you When you use this bonus action, and at the start of each of its turns for the next minute, the creature gains temporary hit points equal to twice your Charisma modifier (minimum 2).

Level 3: Channel Divinity: Share Vitality

As a bonus action, you can take any amount of necrotic damage up to your current number of hit points, which can't be reduced in any way Up to four creatures you can see within 30 feet of you regain hit points equal to half the necrotic damage taken.

Aura of Rejuvenation

You emanate an aura that increases the potency of magical healing and hearty meals Whenever a creature of your choice within 10 feet of you regains hit points from a spell, potion, magical effect, or food, it regains an additional [[/damage 1d6]] hit points*.

When a creature rolls one or more Hit Dice to regain hit points during a short rest, it regains 1 additional hit point for each Hit Dice expended in this way, so long as it spends the majority of the short rest within 10 feet of you.

When you reach 18th level in this class, the range of the aura increases to 30 feet

Lay on Hands & Magic

The paladin's Lay on Hands feature is neither a spell nor a magical effect, thus it does not trigger the bonus healing from the Aura of Rejuvenation.

Host of Heroes

Over the course of an hour (which can be done during a short rest), you can magically create a delicious feast for you and up to nine other creatures, using 25 gp of rare spices and 25 gp of diamond dust Once consumed, a creature that partakes of the feast gains the following benefits for the next 8 hours:

  • The creature has advantage on Constitution saving throws.
  • The creature has resistance to poison damage.
  • The creature is immune to the &Reference[condition=frightened] condition.
  • The creature gains [[/r 2d10]] temporary hit points.

After you use this feature, you can't do so again until you finish a long rest.

Avatar of Nourishment

As a bonus action, you become a wellspring of lifeforce, gaining the following benefits for the next minute:

  • At the start of each of your turns, each creature of your choice within 30 feet of you (including you) regains hit points equal to your Charisma modifier (minimum 1) and gains temporary hit points equal to your Charisma modifier (minimum of 1).
  • As bonus action, you can cast the @spell[revivify] spell without having it prepared and without expending a spell slot (material components are still required).
  • Whenever a creature within 30 feet of you takes damage, you can use your reaction to grant the creature resistance to that damage.

After you use this feature, you can't do so again until you finish a long rest, unless you expend a 5th-level spell slot to use it again.

The tenets of the Oath of the Harvest inspire their followers to seek out potential harm and quell it before it blossoms.

Share Your Meal. Your powers are a gift to be shared; if someone is in need, you must use your power to meet those needs. To eat your fill while another goes hungry is selfish.

Nurture Over Cure. Act in the greatest interest of the many. Find ways to prevent harm before it must be healed.

Permit Prosperity. Whether in matters of love, politics, or war, always give your antagonist the opportunity to change and redeem themselves before casting a fatal judgment. A good meal can serve as the backdrop to such events.
Always keen to fortify others with flavourful food, you've spent hours slicing, dicing, and cooking. You gain proficiency with cook's utensils.

Slaves face great difficulty everywhere they go. Escaped slaves are often on the run if not from their former owners, then certainly from the law. Few are educated or have any practical experience to make a way for themselves. Most have limited social skills which give away their social status. Slavers may notice freemen as "unclaimed property" and try to "claim" them as slaves. People sense a sort of "inferiority" about slaves and freemen, and they will likely either ignore you or boss you around. Many freemen turn to crime to make ends meet and so anyone who doesn't assume you a slave immediately, will likely assume that you are a criminal. If you can ever really leave the slavery mindset knowing what it's like to be a slave, then you can pose as a slave with little difficulty and without raising much suspicion. People seem to do things in front of you that they would normally only do when they are alone.

Session kit — The Castle Comes Down (Session III). A GM kit for the night after the breach, not a filed event; nothing on this sheet changes the canon record. The run-sheet is docs/sessions/bowsers-castle-1035-the-castle-comes-down.md.

One of the two Hammer Bros Bowser carried into a side room under his arms when the throne-room wall burst. The record gives the pair one question between them — does the castle have a self-destruct switch, and if the dragon is taking it anyway, could they not blow it up and walk the survivors to Neo Bowser City? — and does not say which of them asked it. This sheet gives Fred the proposal so the two can be played apart.

Bowser's answer was 'You want me to blow up my own castle?' Fred's position is that Mario once pressed a switch and a whole castle came down, so the technology exists. He is not wrong about the technology. He is a demolitions mind in a hammer-throwing body: his hammers find the weak course in a wall, and he can tell whether a switch does what its label says — which, tonight, matters.

From the record: the side room; the switch question; Mario once pressed a switch and a castle came down.

Built by tools/build-forge-packets.py from the NPC Forge roster data/forge/fawfuls-forces.json (entry fury-bot): Medium construct (Fury-Bot), Unaligned; CR 3 (proficiency +2, to hit +5 with STR); AC 15 (riveted plating and shield), hit points 52 (7d8+21), speed 25 ft.. A GM scene kit for the Fawful's Forces article's present (1040 BF), not a filed event; the faction article stays the authority.

The Fury Meter's fourth rung, in the faction article's own words: "Fury-Bots and the castle's main cannon". Where a Chortle-Bot is tin, a Fury-Bot is boilerplate — a drill, a shield with a grin riveted onto it, and a governor that only has one setting. The occupation uses them as door-openers and as the wall that stands in front of the Bean Garrison when the garrison is reloading.

It is not clever. It will charge the nearest thing, drill it, and keep drilling; the extra damage on a straight 20-foot run is how it kills, so fight it in tight corners, around furniture, or with something prone on the floor between you. The shield guard reaction means the thing standing behind a Fury-Bot is harder to hit than it looks.

A GM scene kit for the Fawful's Forces article's present (1040 BF), not a filed event; the faction article stays the authority.

"Mutate" is the faction article's word; the garrison's is "the vats". A Furybean started as a trooper who volunteered, or did not, for a week in the green tanks under the kitchens, and came out twice the size with a vocabulary of one word. They are kept behind the Fury-Bots until something needs lifting, throwing or breaking, and then they are let go.

The regeneration is the fight: five a turn, forever, unless the party brings cold. Anything frosty — a spell, a wand, a bucket of the castle's own ice-house — shuts it off for a round and the brute is suddenly a big slow bag of hit points. Expect it to grab a small party member and throw them at a large one.

biography.value:
Bandits of our humble world come in a variety of shapes and sizes; be they a halfling pickpocket or the swarthy Dragonborn sea-captain plundering unfortunate vessels. Here we will view the commonalities of what would be considered the “bandit” class of criminal. Be advised while reviewing this information that not all bandits should be viewed with a scornful eye. While many seek harm or riches from their quarry, others thieve to survive in a world most unfair.

The Good. We begin with those bandits who could be seen as “noble criminals”. These bandits consist of the most downtrodden of our nations, those citizens who have struggled through poverty and oppression to scrape out a meager existence clinging to any comfort they can grasp. Consider what would drive a person to commit something so desperate as robbery or open theft in a village street. Bandits of a nobler sort may still be selfish with their earnings, taking what they have stolen to enrich their own lives or those of immediate relations. There are some bandits, however, who seek to use their pilfered goods to improve the lives of the poorer community. Be aware that often these bandits are desperate and afraid, especially during the act of robbery. They are scared, driven to crime by poor circumstances, so they may not require violence to disperse as more often than not they will not physically harm their victims. Keep an open mind as you travel through the world young adventurer and remember that were the tables turned, you may wish for mercy for such a minor infraction.

The Bad and Ugly. For every good-hearted soul stealing from those with too much and giving to the unfortunate, there is a truly villainous spirit lurking behind the brush of a nearby road, lying in wait for an unsuspecting victim. During your travels, adventurer, these sorts may be the most common instances of banditry you will experience. Armed with swords, clubs, and bows, the more nefarious of the bandit world prefer to ambush their prey from the shadows of hills and trees, catching traveling parties unaware. These treacherous thieves will attempt diversion and trickery in order to catch their quarry off guard should their crew be outnumbered. Bandits have no boundaries of borders or locale, so caution should be taken whether you walk upon a forested road or sail the high seas as you island hop for fame. Danger lurks in every corner of our world adventurer, be prepared and discerning should you encounter a party of brigands lest your career end well before your legend is written.

biography.value:
Goomba — The Ones Who Die First

The Goomba is the most common, most expendable, and most tragically undervalued member of the Koopa Troop's military structure. They are small mushroom-like creatures with no arms, stubby legs, prominent eyebrows that convey a permanent expression of mild indignation, and a combat life expectancy measured in seconds against competent opponents. Mario has personally defeated more Goombas than any living being has defeated anything, and the Goomba species has responded to this statistical reality with the kind of resigned determination that characterizes organisms whose survival strategy is volume rather than individual resilience.

Goombas serve as the Troop's conscript infantry—the bodies that fill formations, the patrols that walk corridors, the first wave that absorbs enemy attention while more valuable units position themselves. Their combat contribution is primarily absorptive: they exist to be engaged, to occupy enemy actions, and to die in ways that provide tactical information to the units behind them. "The Goomba learned that the enemy attacks with jumping" is a genuine entry in Koopa Troop tactical manuals, and nobody in the Troop's command structure considers this entry problematic.

The Goombas themselves have complicated feelings about their role. Many serve willingly because the Troop provides community, structure, and the sense of purpose that civilian Goomba life—which consists primarily of walking back and forth on platforms for reasons nobody has ever explained—does not offer. Others serve because conscription offers no alternative. And some serve with the quiet defiance of creatures who know they're cannon fodder and have decided to be the best cannon fodder possible, approaching their inevitable defeats with a professionalism that their commanders don't appreciate and that historians will never record.
biography.public: A small mushroom creature walking a patrol route with an expression of permanent mild annoyance, as though it knows exactly how expendable it is and has opinions about this that nobody asks.

description.value:
The Goomba's only attack is running into enemies headfirst, using its disproportionately hard cranium as a bludgeoning weapon. The headbonk is not sophisticated. It is not elegant. It is a small creature running at you with its head down and hoping that the impact accomplishes something useful. Against unarmored, distracted, or very unlucky targets, it occasionally does.

The headbonk's primary tactical value is distraction rather than damage. A Goomba headbonking an enemy forces that enemy to spend an action dealing with the Goomba rather than engaging more valuable targets. If the enemy stomps the Goomba (which typically requires one attack and deals any amount of damage, since Goombas have 7 hit points and AC 8), the Goomba has accomplished its mission: one enemy action consumed, one moment of tactical advantage created for the unit behind it.

Goombas who survive headbonk attempts are surprised and mildly confused by the experience. Success is not what training prepares them for.
description.chat: It runs at you head-first with the total commitment of someone who has accepted that this is probably the end and has decided to make it count.

unidentified.name: Headbutt
unidentified.description: A small creature charging headfirst with more determination than tactical viability.

description.value:
Goombas are critically vulnerable to attacks from above. Any attack that strikes a Goomba from a higher elevation—jumping attacks, falling objects, dropped items, gravity—deals double damage. This vulnerability is biological: the Goomba's cranium is hard for headbonking purposes but the body beneath is soft and compresses easily under downward force. A single stomp from a creature of Medium size or larger is typically sufficient to defeat a Goomba regardless of the attacker's strength score.

This vulnerability is so well-known that it defines the Goomba's tactical identity. They operate on flat terrain whenever possible. They avoid positions beneath ledges, balconies, or elevated platforms. They cluster together so that stomping one requires landing among the others, creating at least marginal retaliatory opportunity. And they maintain a permanent upward awareness that gives them advantage on Wisdom (Perception) checks to notice threats from above, a survival instinct honed by millennia of being the thing that gets stepped on.
description.chat: Don't stomp on them. They know you want to stomp on them. They've arranged their entire tactical doctrine around the assumption that you will try to stomp on them. Stomp on them anyway because it works every time.

description.value:
Goombas are individually negligible threats. In groups, they become something approaching dangerous through sheer volume—not because individual capability increases but because the number of actions required to eliminate them creates opportunities for more capable allies to capitalize on. When three or more Goombas are within 5 feet of each other and attacking the same target, each Goomba gains advantage on its headbonk attack roll as the collective assault from multiple directions makes effective defense more difficult.

This ability has saved Goomba lives exactly never, but it has delayed enemy advances, consumed enemy resources, and created the momentary distractions that Koopa Troopa squads behind them need to set up effective defensive positions. The Goombas don't know this. They think they're fighting. What they're actually doing is buying time with their bodies, and the Troop's tactical doctrine has been built around this function for so long that nobody questions whether it's ethical.
description.chat: One Goomba is a speedbump. Three Goombas are a slightly taller speedbump. Ten Goombas are a genuine tactical consideration, which is the most a Goomba can aspire to.

description.value:
Goombas are immune to the frightened condition. Not because they're brave—bravery implies a choice between fear and action, and Goombas don't experience that choice. They simply walk forward. They have always walked forward. Walking forward into danger is what Goombas do, the way breathing is what lungs do, the way falling is what dropped objects do. It is not courage. It is nature. And nature doesn't require saving throws.

This immunity makes Goombas unexpectedly useful against enemies who rely on fear effects. Dragon frightful presence, undead horrifying visage, banshee wailing—none of it stops a Goomba. The Goomba continues walking forward with its expression of mild annoyance, headbonking whatever terrifying entity it encounters with the same determination it would apply to a locked door or an unfamiliar obstacle. The Goomba doesn't understand why the dragon is surprised. The Goomba doesn't understand most things. The Goomba walks forward.
description.chat: It's not brave. It's not fearless. It simply doesn't have the cognitive architecture for fear to interrupt its walking-forward subroutine. The dragon is confused. The Goomba is not.

description.value:
You gain the service of a familiar, a spirit that takes an animal form you choose: Bat, Cat, Frog, Hawk, Lizard, Octopus, Owl, Rat, Raven, Spider, Weasel, or another Beast that has a Challenge Rating of 0. Appearing in an unoccupied space within range, the familiar has the statistics of the chosen form (see appendix B), though it is a Celestial, Fey, or Fiend (your choice) instead of a Beast. Your familiar acts independently of you, but it obeys your commands.

Telepathic Connection. While your familiar is within 100 feet of you, you can communicate with it telepathically. Additionally, as a Bonus Action, you can see through the familiar's eyes and hear what it hears until the start of your next turn, gaining the benefits of any special senses it has.

Finally, when you cast a spell with a range of touch, your familiar can deliver the touch. Your familiar must be within 100 feet of you, and it must take a Reaction to deliver the touch when you cast the spell.

Combat. The familiar is an ally to you and your allies. It rolls its own Initiative and acts on its own turn. A familiar can't attack, but it can take other actions as normal.

Disappearance of the Familiar. When the familiar drops to 0 Hit Points, it disappears. It reappears after you cast this spell again. As a Magic action, you can temporarily dismiss the familiar to a pocket dimension. Alternatively, you can dismiss it forever. As a Magic action while it is temporarily dismissed, you can cause it to reappear in an unoccupied space within 30 feet of you. Whenever the familiar drops to 0 Hit Points or disappears into the pocket dimension, it leaves behind in its space anything it was wearing or carrying.

One Familiar Only. You can't have more than one familiar at a time. If you cast this spell while you have a familiar, you instead cause it to adopt a new eligible form.

You touch an object throughout the spell's casting. If the object is a magic item or some other magical object, you learn its properties and how to use them, whether it requires Attunement, and how many charges it has, if any. You learn whether any ongoing spells are affecting the item and what they are. If the item was created by a spell, you learn that spell's name.

If you instead touch a creature throughout the casting, you learn which ongoing spells, if any, are currently affecting it.

Describe or name an object that is familiar to you. You sense the direction to the object's location if that object is within 1,000 feet of you. If the object is in motion, you know the direction of its movement.

The spell can locate a specific object known to you if you have seen it up close—within 30 feet—at least once. Alternatively, the spell can locate the nearest object of a particular kind, such as a certain kind of apparel, jewelry, furniture, tool, or weapon.

This spell can't locate an object if any thickness of lead blocks a direct path between you and the object.

You can see and hear a creature you choose that is on the same plane of existence as you. The target makes a Wisdom saving throw, which is modified (see the tables below) by how well you know the target and the sort of physical connection you have to it. The target doesn't know what it is making the save against, only that it feels uneasy.

Your Knowledge of the Target Is …Save Modifier
Secondhand (heard of the target)+5
Firsthand (met the target)+0
Extensive (know the target well)−5
You Have the Target's …Save Modifier
Picture or other likeness−2
Garment or other possession−4

On a successful save, the target isn't affected, and you can't use this spell on it again for 24 hours.

On a failed save, the spell creates an Invisible, intangible sensor within 10 feet of the target. You can see and hear through the sensor as if you were there. The sensor moves with the target, remaining within 10 feet of it for the duration. If something can see the sensor, it appears as a luminous orb about the size of your fist.

Instead of targeting a creature, you can target a location you have seen. When you do so, the sensor appears at that location and doesn't move.

This spell creates an Invisible, mindless, shapeless, Medium force that performs simple tasks at your command until the spell ends. The servant springs into existence in an unoccupied space on the ground within range. It has AC 10, 1 Hit Point, and a Strength of 2, and it can't attack. If it drops to 0 Hit Points, the spell ends.

Once on each of your turns as a Bonus Action, you can mentally command the servant to move up to 15 feet and interact with an object. The servant can perform simple tasks that a human could do, such as fetching things, cleaning, mending, folding clothes, lighting fires, serving food, and pouring drinks. Once you give the command, the servant performs the task to the best of its ability until it completes the task, then waits for your next command.

If you command the servant to perform a task that would move it more than 60 feet away from you, the spell ends.

biography.value:
Green T — The Giant from the Children's Table

Level 6; Toad (transformation capabilities); independent, formerly of the Tea Leaf Syndicate. A tea merchant who ran a criminal empire with the manners of a garden-party host, and who has never once raised his voice to do it.

The comeback

Green T was lost at the Siege of Raventree Manor when a glass entity took hold of him and pulled him bodily through a mirror. Witnesses agree on the detail that matters: one moment he was there with his feet on solid ground, the next the surface rippled and went still and reflected an empty hallway. He was filed as a casualty.

He came back through the Shadowfell. The route is not established and he has not been forthcoming about it; the working reading is that the mirror dimension is a transit layer between planes rather than a grave. He reappeared at the Shadow Estate dinner intact and ready to cause problems, was seated at the children's table as a deliberate insult, used the insult as cover to map the room, and shot Orangus Cornelius with a silver bullet in front of every vampire lord present.

Since then: custodian of the repaired Mirror of True Reflection under a bargain in which Wario expects to claim it once Scarecrow is dealt with, and a giant observation tower in the grove beyond Tymnas's cottage, where he lifted Remi to his shoulder to spot the Scorncrow and learned in public that the giant form spends the body that holds it.

How he plays

Green T treats a fight as a problem of angles, visibility, and how long a body can hold a shape before the shape starts spending the body back. He is patient to the point that people mistake it for harmlessness, which is the whole method. The giant form is a resource with a cost curve, not a win condition — at the grove the bats swarmed his face until his scale became a disadvantage, more target and not more clarity.

Being underestimated is a weapon. He has never corrected anyone who was wrong about him in a useful direction.
