biography.value:
Magikoopa — The Troop's Magical Backbone

Magikoopas are the Koopa Troop's spellcasters—koopas who discovered magical aptitude and were trained in the traditions that Kamek established centuries ago. They wear blue robes, round spectacles that may or may not be prescription, and pointed hats that serve no magical function but have become traditional enough that going without one is considered professionally inappropriate. They ride broomsticks because Kamek rode a broomstick and tradition is tradition, though several younger Magikoopas have privately expressed interest in more modern transportation methods.

The Magikoopa magical tradition is distinct from the Mages' Guild's approach, from the Beanish magical systems, and from any other structured magical education in the region. Magikoopa magic is innate and species-specific—you either have the aptitude or you don't, and if you do, training refines it into a set of capabilities that includes shape-shifting objects, projectile energy blasts, and the teleportation that makes Magikoopas the Troop's most strategically mobile assets.

Standard Magikoopas serve as the Troop's magical support: healing wounded soldiers, enchanting equipment, providing magical reconnaissance, and—when combat requires it—delivering energy blasts that compensate for the Troop's otherwise limited ranged capability. They are not front-line combatants; their role is support and force multiplication, making other units more effective rather than winning engagements independently.

Kamek's return has energized the Magikoopa corps in ways that concern the Troop's non-magical personnel. The Magikoopas have always been loyal to Kamek before Bowser—he trained them, he established their traditions, he represents the magical heritage that gives their lives meaning. With Bowser absent and Kamek consolidating power, the Magikoopas' divided loyalty has become straightforward loyalty to Kamek, and their capabilities are being deployed according to Kamek's priorities rather than Bowser's standing orders.
biography.public: A robed koopa with round spectacles and a pointed hat, hovering on a broomstick with the dignified irritation of someone whose professional expertise is frequently undervalued by the non-magical soldiers they support.

description.value:
The Magikoopa's primary offensive spell: a shaped blast of magical energy that manifests as a geometric shape—typically a triangle, circle, or square—spinning toward the target with moderate speed and significant force. The shape is cosmetic rather than functional; all blast shapes deal the same damage. The variation exists because Kamek's original training manual included diagrams of different shapes and later generations of Magikoopas assumed each shape was a different spell rather than aesthetic options for the same effect.

The blast can be fired at a target within 60 feet as a ranged spell attack. On a hit, it deals 3d6 force damage. The damage type is force rather than elemental because Magikoopa magic operates on a fundamentally different principle than conventional arcane tradition—it manipulates reality directly rather than channeling elemental energies, which is why the blasts appear as abstract shapes rather than fire, ice, or lightning.
description.chat: A spinning geometric shape—today's shape is triangles—arcs toward the target with the professional precision of someone who has been doing this exact attack for their entire career.

unidentified.name: Geometric Energy Blast
unidentified.description: A ranged magical attack that manifests as spinning geometric shapes, dealing force damage through direct reality manipulation.

description.value:
Magikoopas can transform non-magical, non-attended objects into different objects of similar size and mass. A brick becomes a coin. A barrel becomes a Goomba (temporary, reverts in 1 hour). A rock becomes a mushroom that may or may not be edible depending on the Magikoopa's skill with the particular transformation. The spell requires an action and affects one object within 30 feet that the Magikoopa can see.

The transformations are temporary—lasting 1 hour before reverting—but they're useful for creating improvised resources, confusing enemies, and the specific kind of battlefield modification that turns a corridor full of barrels into a corridor full of hostile Goombas while the enemy is navigating it. The Goombas created this way are real enough to fight, die, and headbonk with genuine commitment to their brief existences, which raises philosophical questions that Magikoopas prefer not to address.
description.chat: The barrel becomes a Goomba. The Goomba walks forward with the resigned determination of its species. In one hour, it will become a barrel again. It does not know this. It does not need to know this.

description.value:
Magikoopas can channel healing energy into wounded allies, restoring hit points through the same reality-manipulation magic that powers their offensive blasts. As an action, a Magikoopa can touch a creature and restore 2d8 + 3 hit points. This healing can be used three times per long rest, after which the Magikoopa's magical reserves need time to regenerate.

Healing magic is the primary reason Magikoopas are valued by the Troop beyond their combat capabilities. Koopa field medicine is otherwise limited to bandages and rest, and having magical healing available during prolonged engagements significantly reduces casualty rates. Magikoopas are instructed to prioritize healing over offensive action when casualties mount, a protocol that some Magikoopas resent (they trained for combat, not nursing) and others embrace (keeping soldiers alive feels more meaningful than adding to the body count).
description.chat: The wounds close under magical attention, reality being convinced that the damage didn't happen through the same principles that throw geometric shapes at enemies.

description.value:
Every Magikoopa rides a broomstick because Kamek rides a broomstick and tradition is tradition. The broomstick provides a fly speed of 30 feet with hover capability, allowing Magikoopas to maintain elevated positions during combat and traverse terrain that ground-bound forces cannot cross. The broomstick is not magical in itself—the flight is powered by the Magikoopa's innate magic channeled through the broom as a focusing implement.

If the broomstick is destroyed (AC 10, 5 HP), the Magikoopa loses flight capability until it can obtain a replacement. Any broom of appropriate size works as a replacement—the magic is in the rider, not the implement—though Magikoopas are oddly particular about bristle quality and handle finish, treating their brooms with the same care that soldiers treat their weapons.
description.chat: The broom shouldn't fly. The koopa on the broom makes it fly anyway. Tradition and magic combine to produce hovering koopas with geometric opinions about combat.

unidentified.description: A broomstick used as a magical flight implement. The magic is in the rider, not the broom, but the rider is particular about broom quality anyway.

The Plumber Who Vanished — Mushroom Kingdom (Former Hero) / Unknown

Status: Missing — Presumed alive, location unknown, last confirmed sighting 1039 BF at the Star Fountain

Mario is—or WAS—the most famous hero in the Mushroom Kingdom. The man who saved Princess Peach countless times before her assassination in 955 BF. The red-capped plumber who could jump higher than physics should allow, who stomped Bowser's schemes into the ground repeatedly, who was so synonymous with heroism that his NAME became a verb. And then, after eighty-five years of diminished appearances and growing silence, he DISAPPEARED entirely. Luigi found him at the Star Fountain. They flew together on wing caps. Luigi said 'Nothing can hurt us... as long as we're together.' And then Mario was GONE again, and Luigi is working alone for the Mages' Guild at Raventree Manor, sucking up ghosts with a vacuum cleaner and refusing to explain ANYTHING. Waluigi has spent considerable effort piecing together what happened. The picture that emerges is worse than a simple disappearance. WAH. The Garden Above the Fire does not return Mario; it makes his absence louder, because Luigi's rescue ends with Luigi asking the brother who is not in the room whether they are still superstars.

Sacred Oaths

Becoming a paladin involves taking vows that commit the paladin to the cause of righteousness, an active path of fighting wickedness. The final oath, taken when he or she reaches 3rd level, is the culmination of all the paladin's training. Some characters with this class don't consider themselves true paladins until they have reached 3rd level and made this oath. For others, the actual swearing of the oath is a formality, an official stamp on what has always been true in the paladin's heart.

@UUID[Compendium.dnd5e.subclasses.Item.sZ86mbX8D5PfYuhl]{Oath of Devotion}

Breaking Your Oath

A paladin tries to hold to the highest standards of conduct, but even the most virtuous paladin is fallible. Sometimes the right path proves too demanding, sometimes a situation calls for the lesser of two evils, and sometimes the heat of emotion causes a paladin to transgress his or her oath.

A paladin who has broken a vow typically seeks absolution from a cleric who shares his or her faith or from another paladin of the same order. The paladin might spend an allnight vigil in prayer as a sign of penitence, or undertake a fast or similar act of self-denial. After a rite of confession and forgiveness, the paladin starts fresh.

If a paladin willfully violates his or her oath and shows no sign of repentance, the consequences can be more serious. At the GM's discretion, an impenitent paladin might be forced to abandon this class and adopt another.

description.value:
The presence of strong evil registers on your senses like a noxious odor, and powerful good rings like heavenly music in your ears. As an action, you can open your awareness to detect such forces. Until the end of your next turn, you know the location of any celestial, fiend, or undead within 60 feet of you that is not behind total cover. You know the type (celestial, fiend, or undead) of any being whose presence you sense, but not its identity (the vampire Count Strahd von Zarovich, for instance). Within the same radius, you also detect the presence of any place or object that has been consecrated or desecrated, as with the @UUID[Compendium.dnd5e.spells.Item.SLxA9QhrggTz0taU]{Hallow} spell.

You can use this feature a number of times equal to 1 + your Charisma modifier. When you finish a long rest, you regain all expended uses.

Your blessed touch can heal wounds. You have a pool of healing power that replenishes when you take a long rest. With that pool, you can restore a total number of hit points equal to your paladin level × 5.

As an action, you can touch a creature and draw power from the pool to restore a number of hit points to that creature, up to the maximum amount remaining in your pool.

Alternatively, you can expend 5 hit points from your pool of healing to cure the target of one disease or neutralize one poison affecting it. You can cure multiple diseases and neutralize multiple poisons with a single use of Lay on Hands, expending hit points separately for each one.

This feature has no effect on undead and constructs.

By 2nd level, you have learned to draw on divine magic through meditation and prayer to cast spells as a cleric does.

Preparing and Casting Spells

The Paladin table shows how many spell slots you have to cast your spells. To cast one of your paladin spells of 1st level or higher, you must expend a slot of the spell's level or higher. You regain all expended spell slots when you finish a long rest.

You prepare the list of paladin spells that are available for you to cast, choosing from the paladin spell list. When you do so, choose a number of paladin spells equal to your Charisma modifier + half your paladin level, rounded down (minimum of one spell). The spells must be of a level for which you have spell slots.

For example, if you are a 5th-level paladin, you have four 1st-level and two 2nd-level spell slots. With a Charisma of 14, your list of prepared spells can include four spells of 1st or 2nd level, in any combination. If you prepare the 1st-level spell cure wounds, you can cast it using a 1st-level or a 2ndlevel slot. Casting the spell doesn't remove it from your list of prepared spells.

You can change your list of prepared spells when you finish a long rest. Preparing a new list of paladin spells requires time spent in prayer and meditation: at least 1 minute per spell level for each spell on your list.

Spellcasting Ability

Charisma is your spellcasting ability for your paladin spells, since their power derives from the strength of your convictions. You use your Charisma whenever a spell refers to your spellcasting ability. In addition, you use your Charisma modifier when setting the saving throw DC for a paladin spell you cast and when making an attack roll with one.

Spell save DC = 8 + your proficiency bonus + your Charisma modifier

Spell attack modifier = your proficiency bonus + your Charisma modifier

Spellcasting Focus

You can use a holy symbol as a spellcasting focus for your paladin spells.

The extra damage is 2d8 for a 1st-level spell slot, plus 1d8 for each spell level higher than 1st, to a maximum of 5d8. The damage increases by 1d8 if the target is an undead or a fiend.

When you roll a 1 or 2 on a damage die for an attack you make with a melee weapon that you are wielding with two hands, you can reroll the die and must use the new roll, even if the new roll is a 1 or a 2. The weapon must have the two-handed or versatile property for you to gain this benefit.

You have served the community where you grew up, standing as its first line of defense against crime. You aren't a soldier, directing your gaze outward at possible enemies. Instead, your service to your hometown was to help police its populace, protecting the citizenry from lawbreakers and malefactors of every stripe.

You might have been part of the City Watch of Waterdeep, the baton-wielding police force of the City of Splendors, protecting the common folk from thieves and rowdy nobility alike. Or you might have been one of the valiant defenders of Silverymoon, a member of the Silverwatch or even one of the magic-wielding Spellguard.

Perhaps you hail from Neverwinter and have served as one of its Wintershield watchmen, the newly founded branch of guards who vow to keep safe the City of Skilled Hands.

Even if you're not city-born or city-bred, this background can describe your early years as a member of law enforcement. Most settlements of any size have their own constables and police forces, and even smaller communities have sheriffs and bailiffs who stand ready to protect their community.

The Oath of the Watchers binds paladins to protect mortal realms from the predations of extraplanar creatures, many of which can lay waste to mortal soldiers. Thus, the Watchers hone their minds, spirits, and bodies to be the ultimate weapons against such threats.

Paladins who follow the Watchers' oath are ever vigilant in spotting the influence of extraplanar forces, often establishing a network of spies and informants to gather information on suspected cults. To a Watcher, keeping a healthy suspicion and awareness about one's surroundings is as natural as wearing armor in battle.
By 3rd level, the divine magic flowing through you makes you immune to disease.

A paladin who assumes the Oath of the Watchers swears to safeguard mortal realms from otherworldly threats.

Vigilance[–]

The threats you face are cunning, powerful, and subversive. Be ever alert for their corruption.

Loyalty[–]

Never accept gifts or favors from fiends or those who truck with them. Stay true to your order, your comrades, and your duty.

Discipline[–]

You are the shield against the endless terrors that lie beyond the stars. Your blade must be forever sharp and your mind keen to survive what lies beyond.

You gain the following Channel Divinity options. See the Sacred Oath class feature for how Channel Divinity works.

You can use your Channel Divinity to invest your presence with the warding power of your faith. As an action, you can choose a number of creatures you can see within 30 feet of you, up to a number equal to your Charisma modifier (minimum of one creature). For 1 minute, you and the chosen creatures have advantage on Intelligence, Wisdom, and Charisma saving throws.

You can use your Channel Divinity to castigate unworldly beings. As an action, you present your holy symbol and each aberration, celestial, elemental, fey, or fiend within 30 feet of you that can hear you must make a Wisdom saving throw. On a failed save, the creature is turned for 1 minute or until it takes damage.

A turned creature must spend its turns trying to move as far away from you as it can, and it can't willingly end its move in a space within 30 feet of you. For its action, it can use only the @action[Dash] action or try to escape from an effect that prevents it from moving. If there's nowhere to move, the creature can take the @action[Dodge] action.

When you reach 3rd level, you swear the oath that binds you as a paladin forever. Up to this time you have been in a preparatory stage, committed to the path but not yet sworn to it. Now you choose from the list of available oaths.

Your choice grants you features at 3rd level and again at 7th, 15th, and 20th level. Those features include oath spells and the Channel Divinity feature.

Oath Spells.

Each oath has a list of associated spells. You gain access to these spells at the levels specified in the oath description. Once you gain access to an oath spell, you always have it prepared. Oath spells don't count against the number of spells you can prepare each day.

If you gain an oath spell that doesn't appear on the paladin spell list, the spell is nonetheless a paladin spell for you.

Breaking Your Oath

[–]

A paladin tries to hold to the highest standards of conduct, but even the most virtuous paladin is fallible. Sometimes the right path proves too demanding, sometimes a situation calls for the lesser of two evils, and sometimes the heat of emotion causes a paladin to transgress his or her oath.

A paladin who has broken a vow typically seeks absolution from a cleric who shares his or her faith or from another paladin of the same order. The paladin might spend an all-night vigil in prayer as a sign of penitence, or undertake a fast or similar act of self-denial. After a rite of confession and forgiveness, the paladin starts fresh.

If a paladin willfully violates his or her oath and shows no sign of repentance, the consequences can be more serious. At the DM's discretion, an impenitent paladin might be forced to abandon this class and adopt another, or perhaps to take the Oathbreaker paladin option that appears in the Dungeon Master's Guide.

Your oath allows you to channel divine energy to fuel magical effects. Each Channel Divinity option provided by your oath explains how to use it.

When you use your Channel Divinity, you choose which option to use. You must then finish a short or long rest to use your Channel Divinity again.

Some Channel Divinity effects require saving throws. When you use such an effect from this class, the DC equals your paladin spell save DC.

The next time you hit with a melee weapon attack during this spell's duration, your attack deals an extra [[/damage 1d6 type=psychic]] damage. Additionally, if the target is a creature, it must make a Wisdom saving throw or be &Reference[condition=frightened] of you until the spell ends. As an action, the creature can make a Wisdom check against your spell save DC to steel its resolve and end this spell.

The next time you hit a creature with a melee weapon attack during the spell's duration, your weapon flares with white-hot intensity, and the attack deals an extra [[/damage 1d6 type=fire]] damage to the target and causes the target to ignite in flames. At the start of each of its turns until the spell ends, the target must make a Constitution saving throw. On a failed save, it takes [[/damage 1d6 type=fire]] damage. On a successful save, the spell ends. If the target or a creature within 5 feet of it uses an action to put out the flames, or if some other effect douses the flames (such as the target being submerged in water), the spell ends.

At Higher Levels.

When you cast this spell using a spell slot of 2nd level or higher, the initial extra damage dealt by the attack increases by [[/damage 1d6]] for each slot level above 1st.

The first time you hit with a melee weapon attack during this spell's duration, your weapon rings with thunder that is audible within 300 feet of you, and the attack deals an extra [[/damage 2d6 type=thunder]] damage to the target. Additionally, if the target is a creature, it must succeed on a Strength saving throw or be pushed 10 feet away from you and knocked &Reference[condition=prone].

A hand-held, portable, two-way radio transceiver. Multiple radios use a single channel, and only one radio on the channel can transmit at a time, although any number can listen. The transceiver is normally in receiving mode and when the user wants to talk he presses a "push-to-talk" button. You can communicate with someone using a two-way radio at the same frequency up to 20 miles.

Wrought from metal in the likeness of a brazier, this ranged weapon's grip has been covered in wax and has a simple candle positioned in front of where the arrow or bolt is fired from. The candle is magic and never runs out of wax, nor can it be removed from the weapon. You can use a bonus action to speak the weapon's command word to cause the candle to light itself, shedding light like a normal candle while ablaze. While the candle is lit, this magic weapon deals an extra 2 fire damage to any target it hits with a ranged attack. The candle's flame lasts until you use a bonus action to speak the command word again or until you drop or stow the weapon.

If you roll the same number on both [[/r d20]]s when you make a ranged attack roll with advantage or disadvantage using this weapon while its candle is lit, the ammunition becomes wreathed in a conflagration of uncontrollable flames. The arrow or bolt flies toward the target and explodes, destroying the ammunition and dealing [[/damage 4d6 type=fire]] damage to the target (instead of the attack's normal damage), or half as much damage if the total of the attack roll was less than the target's AC. This fire ignites flammable objects within 5 feet of the target that aren't being worn or carried. This property can't be used again until the next dawn.

You summon a spirit that assumes the form of an unusually intelligent, strong, and loyal steed, creating a long-lasting bond with it. Appearing in an unoccupied space within range, the steed takes on a form that you choose: a @creature[warhorse], a @creature[pony], a @creature[camel], an @creature[elk], or a @creature[mastiff]. (Your DM might allow other animals to be summoned as steeds.) The steed has the statistics of the chosen form, though it is a celestial, fey, or fiend (your choice) instead of its normal type. Additionally, if your steed has an Intelligence of 5 or less, its Intelligence becomes 6, and it gains the ability to understand one language of your choice that you speak.

Your steed serves you as a mount, both in combat and out, and you have an instinctive bond with it that allows you to fight as a seamless unit. While mounted on your steed, you can make any spell you cast that targets only you also target your steed.

When the steed drops to 0 hit points, it disappears, leaving behind no physical form. You can also dismiss your steed at any time as an action, causing it to disappear. In either case, casting this spell again summons the same steed, restored to its hit point maximum.

While your steed is within 1 mile of you, you can communicate with each other telepathically.

You can't have more than one steed bonded by this spell at a time. As an action, you can release the steed from its bond at any time, causing it to disappear.

A broken half‑ring of blackened gold with a dull, cracked red gem that still pulses faintly with command‑magic. This was once the "handler" half of a paired Entropy Ring system like the one the Iron Legion forced onto Toadburt on Highsun 21, turning him into a coerced sleeper agent with a three‑day deadline to capture the Oracle. Archie managed to snap this handler piece off during his own interrogation by Agent Malissia in the physical antechamber, intending to study it and reverse‑engineer a way to free those bound by the complete rings.

He never got the chance. But even broken, the ring stub retains enough residual magic to sense its paired counterparts and—just once per day—to jam their signal. This is how Archie hoped to give Toadburt one moment of free will, one chance to disobey the Iron Legion's orders and act as himself instead of their puppet. Whether Toadburt ever received that chance, or whether the jamming came too late, is a question the stub cannot answer. It can only pulse with the distant heartbeat of command‑magic still being transmitted somewhere in the world.

While attuned, you can sense if an active Entropy Ring is within 300 feet. You learn only "near" or "farther than that," but not direction or who wears it. Once per day, as an action, you can focus on the stub and attempt to jam an Entropy Ring in range. The bearer of that ring must succeed on a DC 14 Wisdom saving throw or experience 1 round of static in their orders—they know something is wrong and briefly act under their own will instead of their controller's. Each time you use the jamming effect, you must succeed on a DC 12 Constitution save or take 1d6 necrotic damage as the broken magic eats at your fingertips, aging them visibly for a few heartbeats.
description.chat: The cracked gem buzzes with distant command‑magic, like half of a conversation you can barely hear.

unidentified.name: Cracked Red Gem Ring
unidentified.description: A broken half‑circle ring ending in a cracked red stone. It feels heavier than it looks, and the gold has been blackened as though exposed to intense magical discharge. The gem occasionally pulses with a dim internal light, always in irregular rhythms that suggest some kind of coded signal being transmitted to or from an unknown source.

description.value:
A rolled‑up parchment, singed at the edges and smelling faintly of sulfur, depicting the destroyed Raventree greenhouse in meticulous top‑down view. Tiny colored ink circles mark where each rust monster died, with precise measurements of blast radii, casualty vectors, and structural collapse patterns. The corner is labeled in Archie's increasingly frantic hand: 'Proof this was Tactically Justified.' This is the "evidence" Archie compiled immediately after the Greenhouse Inferno on Highsun 17, attempting to retroactively prove that his overcharged Fireball was the only way to save the party from the rust monster swarm.

He referenced this document when he went on Wahbook on Highsun 20 to publicly confess and justify his actions, arguing with cold mathematical precision that he had saved more lives than he'd taken. The diagram is half combat analysis—noting optimal engagement angles and acceptable casualty thresholds—and half self‑absolution, with margin notes like "No other option" and "They would have done the same." The Mages' Guild saw it as damning evidence of reckless endangerment. The Liberated Toads saw themselves marked as "acceptable collateral." Archie saw it as proof he was right, even if being right cost him everything.

A spellcaster who spends a short rest studying the diagram can apply its cold tactical lessons once: the next time they cast an area fire spell, they can choose any number of creatures up to their spellcasting modifier to automatically succeed on the save against that spell, though they still take half damage. Any Liberated Toad who sees their own location marked as "acceptable collateral" must succeed on a DC 12 Wisdom save or be consumed by anger toward Archie's memory for the rest of the day, unable to speak positively of him or his actions.
description.chat: Colored blast‑circles, casualty marks, and tiny scribbles — the greenhouse as seen through Archie's cold, tactical eye.

unidentified.name: Scorched Floorplan
unidentified.description: A partially burned blueprint of a glass‑roofed building, annotated with circles and numbers in multiple colors of ink. The draftsmanship is precise despite the damage, and small notations in cramped handwriting fill every available margin. Scorch marks along the edges suggest this document was itself present during whatever fire it depicts, and you can still smell smoke when you unroll it.

description.value:
A tarnished brass circlet lined with a strip of stiff, dried leather that bears the faint chemical smell of alchemical preservation. On the inside, written in Archie's cramped ink, is a desperate mantra: 'The eye sees across – the band keeps me from falling in.' Faint grooves mark where the metal dug into his brow during the unstable Third Eye Escape on Highsun 20, when he traversed alien dimensions to evade capture. The band itself vibrates faintly when brought near mirrors or planar boundaries, as though resonating with tears in reality.

This circlet represents Archie's personal safeguard against the very magic he studied. After encountering his own two‑eyed clone in the sewers beneath the restaurant on Highsun 14—a clone desperate to steal his third eye for the Iron Legion's necromancers—Archie became obsessed with protecting his mind from dimensional fracture. The band is his answer: crude, painful, but effective. It kept him anchored during his escape through the Deep Layers and prevented the Oracle's fractured visions from consuming him entirely during the Shattered Ritual.

While attuned and worn, you gain a +1 bonus to Intelligence (Arcana) checks and Wisdom (Perception) checks involving portals, planar anomalies, mirrors, or time distortions. Once per long rest, when you would suffer a teleportation mishap, become Banished, or be pulled into an extra‑dimensional space against your will, you can use your reaction to negate that effect for yourself. Each time you use this reaction, you gain one level of Short‑Term Madness as you momentarily see the fractured timelines the way Archie did—Physical, Shadow, Fey, and Deep Mirror all overlapping in impossible geometries.
description.chat: The band squeezes around your temples, and for a second the room triple‑exposes into Physical, Mirror, and Deep Layers before snapping back.

unidentified.name: Tight Brass Circlet
unidentified.description: A plain brass band, slightly warped, with ink‑scribbles along the inner rim. It feels uncomfortable, like it's meant to be too tight. The leather lining is stiff and cracked, and there are faint pressure marks on the inside as though someone wore this for extended periods despite the discomfort. When you hold it up to the light, the brass seems to shimmer with an oil‑slick iridescence.

The Rotting Skull Piercer is a nightmarish warhammer forged from the calcified skull of an ancient lich, its surface etched with arcane runes that pulse with a sickly green ichor. When wielded, it unleashes waves of decaying energy that corrode both flesh and metal, leaving nothing but bone behind. Its touch is said to spread rot through the very air, making those who hold it feel as though their own vitality is being consumed.

Effects

  • Rotting Decay: On activation, the Rotting Skull Piercer unleashes a wave of decaying energy that deals 100 points of damage over five turns. The target must make a DC 18 Constitution saving throw or be affected by the 'Rotting' status effect, which reduces their armor class by 2 until the end of their next turn.
  • Armor Corrosion: Each time you hit with this weapon, there is a 30% chance that the target is also inflicted with 'Weakness,' reducing its Strength score by 1 for one minute. This effect stacks up to three times per encounter.

Usage

  • Activation: Action
  • Duration: Instantaneous effect over five turns
  • Ends when: The target successfully saves against Rotting Decay or the weapon is used again on a different target.
  • Charges: Unlimited, recharged at dawn

The Skullsplitter Warhammer, forged from the bones of fallen soldiers, exudes a dark, almost sentient power. Its haft is reinforced with iron bands and its head is adorned with an ancient rune that whispers malevolent secrets to those who wield it. This weapon guarantees a crushing blow, capable of turning the strongest foe into dust with each strike. However, those who use it must beware, for it seems to have a mind of its own, often striking out at unintended targets in its fervor to destroy.

Effects

  • Crushing Blow: When you make a melee attack with the Skullsplitter Warhammer, it deals an additional 1d6 bludgeoning damage. If the target is reduced to half its hit points or fewer by this weapon, there is a 50% chance that they bleed out and take an additional 1d4 necrotic damage at the start of their next turn.
  • Sentient Wrath: At the end of each of your turns while wielding the Skullsplitter Warhammer, there is a 25% chance that it will lash out and target an enemy within 5 feet of you. This attack deals 1d8 bludgeoning damage and has disadvantage if you are concentrating or using an action.

Usage

  • Activation: As a bonus action
  • Duration: Until the start of your next turn
  • Ends when: You sheathe it or drop the weapon, or if you take an action other than moving
  • Charges: Unlimited

biography.value:
Midbus — Fawful's Fist, Bowser's Replacement

Midbus is the creature Fawful built to be Bowser's opposite. Where Bowser is fire, Midbus is ice. Where Bowser is prideful rage, Midbus is cold obedience. Where Bowser fights for his own glory, Midbus fights because Fawful tells him to fight. He is a massive pig-beast of uncertain origin—part mechanical, part organic, part something that Fawful's engineering produced through processes that conventional biology finds objectionable—and he serves as Fawful's primary enforcer, bodyguard, and blunt instrument for situations that require something larger than bombs and more reliable than dragons.

The relationship between Midbus and Fawful is the inverse of the relationship between Bowser and his Koopa Troop. The Koopa Troop follows Bowser because he's powerful and because loyalty to the king is tradition. Midbus follows Fawful because Fawful MADE him. Not in the biological sense—Midbus existed before Fawful found him—but in every functional sense. Fawful took something large, stupid, and violent and gave it purpose, direction, and the modifications necessary to become something genuinely dangerous rather than merely big. Without Fawful, Midbus would be an animal. With Fawful, Midbus is a weapon that happens to have a personality, though the personality consists primarily of loyalty and the desire to hit things hard enough that they stop moving.

Midbus's modifications are extensive and not entirely visible. The ice capabilities that define his combat style are not natural—they were installed by Fawful using technology derived from the Dark Star fragment and Beanish cryogenic engineering that was considered too dangerous for military application by the Beanbean Kingdom's regulators. Fawful didn't care about regulators. Fawful cared about results. The result is a creature that can generate freezing temperatures from its body, project ice in offensive formations, and sustain itself in environments that would kill organic beings through cold alone.

The "Blizzard Fist" designation is Fawful's invention—he names everything, he names it dramatically, and he expects the names to be used. Midbus doesn't care about the name. Midbus doesn't care about most things. He cares about following Fawful's orders, eating large quantities of food, and proving that he is stronger than Bowser. The last motivation is the only one that produces genuine emotional response—when Bowser's name is mentioned, Midbus's normally placid demeanor shifts to something approaching engagement, and his already considerable aggression intensifies to levels that make Fawful's other operatives nervous.

The rivalry with Bowser predates Fawful's current operation. During the Dark Star Crisis—an event that official records minimize even more aggressively than they minimize the Chaos Heart Crisis—Midbus and Bowser fought repeatedly, each encounter escalating in destruction and personal animosity. Midbus won some of these fights. Bowser won others. Neither achieved the decisive victory that would end the rivalry, and both carry the frustration of unfinished business that only another fight can resolve.

Currently, Midbus serves as the garrison commander of Peach's Castle under Fawful's occupation. He manages the five hundred-plus troops, maintains order among personnel whose loyalty to Fawful varies from genuine devotion to practical opportunism, and deals with the logistical challenges of occupying a castle that was designed for royal residence rather than military fortification. His management style is straightforward: follow orders or be hurt. The simplicity works because Midbus can back it up, and because soldiers who've seen what happens to people who disobey Midbus tend to become enthusiastic followers very quickly.

The four Operation HOMECOMING operatives embedded in Fawful's servant staff operate under Midbus's garrison command without his knowledge. If he discovered them, the response would not involve interrogation or political calculation. It would involve Midbus picking them up and throwing them into walls until the walls or the operatives stopped being solid. Midbus doesn't do subtlety. Midbus does kinetic problem-solving, and he considers most problems solvable if you apply enough kinetic energy to them.

If the party encounters Midbus—through the HOMECOMING operation, through direct assault on Peach's Castle, or through the chaotic convergences that have characterized the current crisis—they will face something that combines the raw physical power of a creature designed to match Bowser with the cold-based enhancement of Fawful's forbidden engineering. He is not clever. He is not subtle. He is not interested in conversation beyond confirming that you are an enemy and therefore something to be frozen and broken.

He is, however, loyal. Absolutely, unquestioningly, terminally loyal to Fawful. This loyalty is Midbus's defining characteristic and his most dangerous quality, because it means he will never stop, never negotiate, never question orders, and never accept defeat while Fawful's will requires him to fight. He is the blunt instrument that Fawful's sharp mind deploys when precision has finished its work and what remains requires force.
biography.public: A massive pig-beast wreathed in frost, standing with the planted solidity of something that has been designed to absorb punishment and return it multiplied. His eyes carry the dull patience of someone who is waiting for permission to destroy something.

description.value:
Midbus's primary weapons are his fists—enormous, frost-coated, and capable of delivering impacts that combine raw physical force with cryogenic damage that freezes tissue on contact. The frost isn't external coating; it radiates from within Midbus's modified physiology, generated by the Beanish cryogenic systems that Fawful installed during the modification process. The frost forms continuously, creating a visible layer of ice crystals on Midbus's knuckles that shatters on impact and reforms between punches.

Each strike delivers bludgeoning damage from the physical impact plus cold damage from the cryogenic effect. Targets hit must contend with the freezing effect—the cold numbs flesh, slows reactions, and can immobilize limbs if sustained exposure accumulates. Watching Midbus fight is like watching an avalanche with opinions: large, cold, absolutely committed to reaching the bottom regardless of what's in the way.
description.chat: Frost-coated fists the size of dinner plates swing with force that promises broken bones and frostbite delivered simultaneously.

unidentified.name: Frost-Generating Fists
unidentified.description: Enormous fists that radiate cold from within, delivering both physical and cryogenic damage on impact.

description.value:
Midbus can hurl his considerable mass at enemies, launching himself across distances that something his size shouldn't be able to cover and landing with impact that shakes the ground. The body slam is his answer to enemies who attempt to maintain distance—ranged attackers, spellcasters, anyone who thinks being far away from the pig-beast makes them safe. It doesn't. Nothing makes you safe from something that weighs half a ton and is willing to use itself as a projectile.

As an action, Midbus can move up to 30 feet in a straight line and slam into a creature at the end of the movement. The target must make a DC 19 Strength saving throw. On a failure, the target takes 4d10 + 7 bludgeoning damage plus 2d8 cold damage, is knocked prone, and is pushed 15 feet away from Midbus. On a success, the target takes half damage and is not knocked prone or pushed. The ground in a 10-foot radius around the impact point becomes difficult terrain covered in frost until the end of Midbus's next turn.
description.chat: Half a ton of frozen pig-beast leaves the ground, crosses distance that should be safe, and lands on you. The ground cracks. You crack. The frost seals the cracks shut.

unidentified.name: Devastating Charge
unidentified.description: This creature can launch itself at enemies over significant distance, delivering devastating impact enhanced with cold damage.

description.value: Midbus makes three Blizzard Fist attacks, or one Body Slam and one Blizzard Fist attack. He can replace one Blizzard Fist attack with a Frost Breath if it's available.
description.chat: Three impacts in rapid succession, each one cold enough to freeze and heavy enough to shatter what it freezes.

description.value:
Midbus exhales a blast of supercooled air in a 40-foot cone, freezing everything in its path. The breath isn't natural—it's generated by the cryogenic systems Fawful installed, channeled through Midbus's respiratory system and expelled with the force of his massive lungs. The temperature drops so dramatically that moisture in the air crystallizes instantly, creating a visible cloud of ice particles that obscures vision and coats everything in frost.

Each creature in the cone must make a DC 19 Constitution saving throw. On a failure, a creature takes 10d8 cold damage and has its speed reduced to 0 until the end of its next turn as frost encases its legs and lower body. On a success, a creature takes half damage and its speed is reduced by half instead of being eliminated. Objects in the cone that aren't being worn or carried freeze solid—water becomes ice, metal becomes brittle, organic material crystallizes and can be shattered by subsequent impacts.

The breath weapon's recharge is mechanical rather than biological—the cryogenic systems need time to build sufficient cold before another discharge. The charging process produces visible condensation around Midbus's mouth and a low humming from the systems in his modified chest cavity, warning observant enemies that the breath is about to happen again.
description.chat: Cold erupts from his mouth in a wave that turns air to crystal, water to stone, and courage to the sudden realization that you should have stood somewhere else.

description.value:
Midbus's body continuously generates a layer of ice that forms over his skin, creating natural armor that regenerates as fast as it's broken. The ice is approximately two inches thick at its heaviest points—shoulders, chest, skull—and provides substantial protection against physical attacks. Weapons that strike Midbus often lodge in the ice rather than penetrating to flesh, requiring the attacker to wrench them free while Midbus is already swinging his next attack.

The cryogenic armor provides AC 18 (natural armor) and grants immunity to cold damage as the ice layer absorbs and disperses freezing effects harmlessly. However, the armor creates vulnerability to fire damage—heat melts the ice faster than it can reform, temporarily reducing Midbus's protection and causing the cryogenic systems to overwork in an attempt to compensate. Fire damage against Midbus is doubled, and for 1 round after taking fire damage, his AC decreases by 2 as the armor thins.

The ice also makes Midbus's surroundings cold. Creatures within 5 feet of Midbus at the start of their turn take 1d6 cold damage from proximity to his frozen exterior, and the ground within 10 feet of his position becomes lightly frosted, requiring careful footing from creatures not accustomed to icy surfaces.
description.chat: Ice forms over his body like a second skin, cracking and reforming with each impact, turning him into something that's more glacier than pig.

description.value:
Midbus's only genuine emotional investment beyond loyalty to Fawful is his rivalry with Bowser. The rivalry is visceral, personal, and rooted in the fundamental question of which creature is the supreme physical force in the Mushroom Kingdom's sphere of influence. Midbus was designed to be Bowser's equal and opposite: ice to fire, obedience to pride, cold efficiency to burning rage. Every fight between them has been inconclusive, and the lack of resolution gnaws at Midbus in ways that nothing else reaches.

When Midbus encounters Bowser or learns of Bowser's presence nearby, his behavior changes. The dull patience that normally characterizes his demeanor sharpens into focused aggression. His attacks become more powerful but less disciplined—advantage on damage rolls, disadvantage on attack rolls—as the desire to prove superiority overrides the mechanical precision that Fawful's modifications normally provide. He will prioritize engaging Bowser over any other objective, including Fawful's orders, which represents the only circumstance under which Midbus's loyalty to Fawful takes second place to personal motivation.

Fawful knows about this vulnerability and has historically exploited it—using Bowser's presence as bait to position Midbus where Fawful needs him, channeling the rivalry's energy toward strategic objectives. Whether Fawful considers the rivalry a useful tool or a concerning limitation in his most valuable enforcer is unclear. Knowing Fawful, the answer is probably both.
description.chat: Bowser's name lands in his ears and something behind the dull eyes ignites—the only fire this frozen creature carries, burning with the need to prove who is strongest.

description.value:
Once per day, Midbus can overclock his cryogenic systems, transforming into a larger, more heavily armored version of himself encased in thick ice that extends his reach and amplifies his cold-generating capabilities. The transformation takes 1 round, during which Midbus cannot take actions or reactions as the ice builds around him in layers. The resulting Blizzard Form lasts for 1 minute.

In Blizzard Form, Midbus's size increases from Large to Huge. His reach increases from 5 feet to 10 feet. His Blizzard Fist damage increases to 3d10 + 7 bludgeoning plus 3d8 cold. His Cryogenic Armor's AC increases to 20. The proximity cold damage increases to 2d6 and extends to 10 feet. And he gains an additional ability: at the start of each of his turns, he creates a 20-foot radius area of extreme cold centered on himself. Each creature in the area must make a DC 19 Constitution saving throw or take 3d6 cold damage and have its speed reduced by 10 feet until the end of its next turn.

After Blizzard Form ends, Midbus's cryogenic systems need time to recalibrate. For 1 minute following the transformation's end, his AC decreases by 4, he loses cold immunity (gaining only resistance), and his Frost Breath cannot recharge. This vulnerability period is the window during which skilled opponents can exploit the overclocked systems' aftermath.
description.chat: Ice builds around him in layers—thicker, colder, MORE—until what stands there isn't a pig-beast anymore but a walking blizzard with fists and the intent to use them.

description.value:
Midbus is immune to all magical effects that would compel him to act against Fawful's interests. Charm Person, Dominate Monster, Suggestion, magical persuasion of any kind—nothing works if the commanded action would harm Fawful, betray Fawful's plans, or compromise Fawful's objectives. This isn't magical protection; it's the absolute loyalty of a creature whose entire identity was constructed around service to one individual. Midbus doesn't resist control because he's protected. He resists because disobeying Fawful is literally inconceivable to him—the neural pathways for independent decision-making regarding Fawful simply don't exist.

This loyalty makes Midbus the most reliable enforcer in the current crisis. He will not betray. He will not negotiate. He will not change sides, accept bribes, or respond to appeals to self-interest because his self-interest IS Fawful's interest. The only circumstance under which this loyalty wavers is the Bowser rivalry, and even that waiver is temporary—after the fight ends, Midbus returns to Fawful's service without question.

The loyalty also represents Midbus's greatest weakness against parties who understand it. Midbus will follow Fawful's orders even when those orders are tactically unsound, because evaluating orders for soundness requires independent judgment that Midbus doesn't possess. Fawful's genius compensates for this limitation under normal circumstances, but if Fawful is incapacitated, distracted, or making mistakes due to his own emotional compromises (the Green Mustache grudge, for example), Midbus will execute bad orders with the same commitment he brings to good ones.
description.chat: He follows because following is what he is. Not what he does—what he IS. Remove Fawful and what remains isn't a rebel. It's a weapon without a hand to aim it.

description.value:
Midbus serves as garrison commander of Peach's Castle, managing 500+ troops through a command style that prioritizes simplicity over sophistication. His orders are clear, his expectations are straightforward, and his consequences for failure are painful. This approach produces a garrison that is disciplined through fear rather than loyalty, competent at following instructions but incapable of independent adaptation when instructions don't cover the situation.

As a bonus action, Midbus can issue a command to garrison soldiers within 60 feet. Soldiers who hear the command gain advantage on their next attack roll or saving throw as they respond to their commander's direction with the urgent compliance of people who know what happens when Midbus is disappointed.

Midbus's garrison management has one significant blind spot: he doesn't look for infiltrators. Servants, maintenance workers, and support staff are beneath his notice. He focuses on soldiers because soldiers are what he understands. The HOMECOMING operatives embedded in Fawful's servant staff operate directly under his command structure, invisible because Midbus has never thought to question whether the people preparing his meals might have agendas beyond food preparation.
description.chat: He commands through the simplest possible principle: do what I say or I will make you wish you had. The principle works. The blind spots it creates might get him killed.

description.value: Twice per day, when Midbus fails a saving throw, he can choose to succeed instead. His modified physiology and the cryogenic systems' integration with his nervous system provide resilience against effects that would stop organic creatures. He pushes through magical compulsion through stubbornness rather than sophistication—his mind is too simple to be redirected and too committed to be overridden.
description.chat: The spell hits. The spell should work. Midbus doesn't care about should. Midbus shrugs it off and keeps coming.

description.value:
Midbus can take 3 legendary actions, choosing from the options below. Only one legendary action can be used at a time and only at the end of another creature's turn.

Frost Stomp (1 action): Midbus stomps the ground, creating a 10-foot radius of ice centered on himself. Each creature in the area must succeed on a DC 17 Dexterity saving throw or fall prone. The ice persists as difficult terrain for 1 round.

Ice Throw (1 action): Midbus tears a chunk of ice from his own armor and hurls it at a target within 60 feet. Ranged attack: +11 to hit, 2d8 + 7 bludgeoning damage plus 1d8 cold damage.

Charge (2 actions): Midbus moves up to his speed toward a target and makes one Blizzard Fist attack at the end of the movement. If the attack hits, the target must succeed on a DC 19 Strength saving throw or be knocked prone.

Frozen Rage (3 actions): Midbus plants himself and swings his fists in a 15-foot radius around himself. Each creature in the area must make a DC 19 Dexterity saving throw, taking 2d10 + 7 bludgeoning damage plus 2d8 cold damage on a failure, or half on a success. After using this action, Midbus cannot take legendary actions until the start of his next turn.
description.chat: Between other creatures' turns, the ice moves—stomping, throwing, charging, raging—a frozen engine of violence that doesn't wait for its own turn to cause destruction.

description.value:
If Fawful is killed, incapacitated, or otherwise removed from the picture, Midbus does not adapt. He does not develop independent objectives. He does not become his own agent. He becomes a weapon without a wielder—still dangerous, still powerful, but without direction, without purpose, without the organizing intelligence that transformed him from animal into enforcer.

Without Fawful's orders, Midbus defaults to the last instructions he received and follows them until they become impossible, then stands still and waits for new instructions that will never come. If no instructions are available, he reverts to territorial behavior: defending whatever location he's currently in against all comers, attacking anything that enters his space, eating whatever is available, and slowly becoming less and less distinguishable from the unintelligent beast he was before Fawful found him.

This regression is neither instant nor inevitable—if someone else assumes command authority that Midbus accepts (which would require either fooling him into believing they speak for Fawful or demonstrating power sufficient to establish new loyalty), he could be redirected. But establishing new loyalty in a creature whose identity is built around one specific person is extraordinarily difficult. Fawful didn't just give Midbus orders. Fawful gave Midbus a SELF. Without Fawful, the self dissolves, and what remains is meat and ice and nothing else.
description.chat: Without the mind that aimed him, the weapon doesn't rebel. It doesn't adapt. It simply stops being a weapon and starts being a thing—large, cold, and waiting for someone who isn't coming back.

The quiet part of the operation. Mimbus stood beside the false heir, close enough to the garrison sheet to read it, threw up a shield when Cackletta's first spell crossed the throne room, shouted for the inner guard and got three answers from the wrong side of the wall. Bowser swiped at him in the courtyard and he fell; he was back at Fawthful's side for the claim at the gate.

If Session III continues from that moment: start Mimbus at half hit points and prone, crawling toward Fawthful. He knows every door that was moved, every defender who was removed without a replacement name, and the passage from the lower barracks to the inner wall that only a traitor could have opened from inside. He is the sheet to capture.

The archive does not assign Mimbus a species; the art is a Goomba in a suit and the sheet follows the art without filing it.

From the record: the shield in the throne room; the swipe in the courtyard; the broken gate.

description.value: Melee, 5 feet. A reinforced briefcase with the castle's routes in it.

When Mimbus or an ally within 10 feet of him is hit by an attack or targeted by a spell, Mimbus raises a shield: the attack has a −4 penalty to hit against the target, or the spell's damage to the target is halved.

Mimbus can open or close any door, gate, or portcullis in Bowser's Castle within 10 feet as a bonus action. He knows where the altered routes on the garrison sheet lead; a creature that reads the sheet (prop_castle_betrayal_roster) and succeeds on a DC 14 Intelligence (Investigation) check learns the same.

While a louder ally — Fawthful, the dragon, the Jester — is acting within 30 feet, Mimbus is unnoticed unless a creature succeeds on a DC 14 Wisdom (Perception) check at the start of its turn. His first attack against a creature that has not noticed him has advantage.
When Mimbus drops below 15 hit points, he becomes invisible until the end of his next turn and may move his speed without provoking opportunity attacks. He is still in the castle.

Mr. L is either Luigi's darkest chapter or Luigi's truest self, depending on who you ask and how much you trust the official narrative. The Regency claims Mr. L was a temporary condition—Luigi brainwashed by dimensional forces, used as a weapon against the Mushroom Kingdom, eventually freed and returned to normal. The warrant charging Luigi with 'residual Mr. L activities' suggests the Regency does not fully believe their own story. The Loyalists claim Mr. L proves Luigi was always compromised and should never be trusted. Luigi himself went SILENT when asked if Mr. L did something evil—a silence witnessed by multiple parties at the ruined manor convergence. Waluigi has spent considerable effort investigating the Mr. L incident, and what Waluigi has found raises more questions than it answers. Was Luigi truly a puppet with someone else pulling the strings? Was Mr. L a separate personality that emerged under stress? Was the 'brainwashing' actually an AWAKENING of something that was always present? And most disturbingly—does Mr. L's existence connect to Mario's disappearance in ways that no one wants to acknowledge? Waluigi does not know. Waluigi is not sure anyone knows. But Waluigi is going to document every theory, every fragment of evidence, and every disturbing implication until the truth emerges or Waluigi runs out of paper. WAH.

Fawful's hatred of mustard is a matter of record — the rants are quoted in the faction article — and the Mustard Sprayer is the revenge he took on it: a boiler of the stuff on treads, aimed at other people. biography.value:
Era sheet: 18 Harvestide, 1035 BF, Bowser's Castle. Art and stats describe this figure on the night the castle came down (events.json bowser_throne_room_compromise and the_assault_on_bowsers_castle), not the present day of the campaign (1040 BF).

Session kit — The Castle Comes Down (Session III). A GM kit for the night after the breach, not a filed event; nothing on this sheet changes the canon record. The run-sheet is docs/sessions/bowsers-castle-1035-the-castle-comes-down.md.

Not a separate person. Omega Bowser is what happens when Bowser's Castle lands on Bowser. The present-day Bowser is a player character at level 8 in the XP ledger; this sheet is his second form for one night, built Gargantuan because the GM asked for a Bowser that is big when the walls come in.

The trigger. When Bowser (the PC) would be reduced to 0 hit points by bludgeoning damage from a collapsing floor or wall, from a falling tower, or from the crush of a Huge or larger creature — the dragon's Wall Breaker, the Switch Hag's countdown, Fawthful dropping the gallery — the GM may call the Omega instead of unconsciousness. The rubble heaves; the thing that stands up fills the room.

The swap. In Foundry, right-click Bowser's token → Transform and drop this sheet on him (keep mental scores), or swap the token for a 4×4 Omega token and run this sheet beside his. Omega starts at full hit points, in the space where Bowser was buried, with his own Legendary Resistances.

The clock. The form lasts 10 rounds, or until Omega Bowser drops to 0 hit points. Then Bowser comes back in the nearest free space: prone, with 1 hit point plus his Constitution modifier for each round the Omega lasted, and one level of exhaustion. Anything Omega was holding falls free. Nothing else carries back.

CR 14 is deliberate: for ten rounds he outclasses the dragon (CR 12) and Fawthful (CR 9) together, which is the point of being crushed by your own castle. He is not a tool for the rest of the campaign.

From the record: Bowser's fire breath and ground pound in the courtyard; the wall that finally burst; a king who kept going back to the breach.

description.value: Melee, reach 15 feet. A Large or smaller creature hit must succeed on a DC 20 Strength saving throw or be pushed 15 feet away and knocked prone.
Melee, reach 10 feet. Plus 2d6 fire damage from the furnace behind the teeth.
Omega Bowser makes two Omega Fist attacks, or one Omega Fist and one Bite.

A 90-foot line 10 feet wide, or a 60-foot cone. Each creature in the area makes a DC 19 Dexterity saving throw, taking 14d6 fire damage on a failure or half as much on a success. Portcullises melt, banners go, the floor glows for a round (difficult terrain, 1d6 fire to anything that ends its turn on it).

Omega Bowser tears a piece of his own castle off his shoulders and throws it: range 60/240, a 20-foot-radius point of impact. Each creature in the area makes a DC 19 Dexterity saving throw, taking 8d10 bludgeoning damage on a failure or half as much on a success; the area becomes difficult terrain. A Huge or smaller flying creature hit by it (the dragon, a hoverpad) falls.

Omega Bowser cannot be knocked prone by a creature smaller than Huge, and he ignores difficult terrain made of rubble. Whenever he moves 10 or more feet inside a built space, the walls and floor he passes through give way: those squares become difficult terrain, and each Medium or smaller creature in them makes a DC 16 Dexterity saving throw, taking 2d10 bludgeoning damage on a failure or half on a success. He deals double damage to objects and structures.

See the biography: trigger (buried at 0 hit points), swap (Transform or token swap, full hit points), clock (10 rounds or 0 hit points), and what comes back (Bowser, prone, 1 hit point + Constitution modifier per round the Omega lasted, one level of exhaustion).
If Omega Bowser fails a saving throw, he can choose to succeed instead.

Omega Bowser can take 3 legendary actions, choosing from the options below, only at the end of another creature's turn, regaining them at the start of his turn.

  • Fist. One Omega Fist attack.
  • Roar. Each hostile creature within 60 feet that can hear him makes a DC 17 Wisdom saving throw or is frightened until the end of its next turn. The supplied dragon is not immune; Fawthful rolls at disadvantage, because for once the bean is not the loudest thing in the room.
  • Stomp (Costs 2 Actions). Each creature on the ground within 20 feet makes a DC 20 Strength saving throw or takes 3d8 bludgeoning damage and is knocked prone. The floor below takes the same.
The Onyx Knights of the Shadeward Manor are clad head-to-toe in onyx plate armor. If a Knight is destroyed, its armor dissolves to dark smoke which seeps downwards into the floor.
The knight makes two melee attacks.

Melee Weapon Attack: +6 to hit, 5 ft., one target. Hit: 10 (1d8 + 4) slashing damage.

The Onyx Knight attacks with its shadowy longsword.

Ranged Weapon Attack: +6 to hit, range 30/60 ft., one target. Hit: 10 (1d10 + 4) cold damage.

The Knight wreaths their blade in shadow and slashes through the air, sending a wave of biting, unnatural cold at their enemy.

The Onyx Knight utters an unintelligible command or warning to an ally it can see within 30 feet. That ally gains an additional +1d4 situational bonus to its next Attack Roll, or Ability Check.

A creature can benefit from only one Dark Guidance die at a time.

Recharges on a 5+ roll of 1d6.

The Onyx Knight adds 2 to its AC against one melee Attack that would hit it.

To do so, the knight must see the attacker and be wielding a melee weapon.
The Onyx Knights of the Shadeward Manor have circular shields made out of dark metal. If a Knight dies, its shield dissolves into black smoke which seeps downwards into the floor.
The Onyx Knight has advantage on saving throws against any effects that turn undead.

Status: Active (Barely) — Shot with silver, tackled out a window, and deeply humiliated

Orangus Cornelius was the senior vampire lord of the Shadow Estate and a figure of absolute authority. Then Green T shot him with a silver bullet from the children's table. Unfortunately, Cornelius survived. Instead of dying gracefully, he turned into a giant bat, got tackled through a window by Bowser, and watched his precious dimensional Anchor get shattered. Waluigi considers surviving this sequence of events physically impressive but socially fatal.

Status: Active — wielding influence within the Iron Fists Guild through her mother Commander G

X.O. is Commander G's daughter and a destabilizing influence within the Iron Fists Guild's Swiftsoul Chapter. She exhibits profound narcissistic entitlement, a god complex that would embarrass actual deities, and a tendency to view Guild operations as theatrical performances staged for her personal amusement. Her demands for dramatic, often cruel, operational protocols may be responsible for the chaotic nature of the Swiftsoul incident—including the elaborate framing of Archie Miser.

The Great Brother of Snowdin — Snowdin Puzzle Guard

Status: Active — recorded in the Snowdin household registry

Sans's taller brother and Snowdin's irrepressible puzzle guard. He treats every visitor as a future friend, every hallway as a stage, and every pot of pasta as a diplomatic instrument. Papyrus is the family's visible heart: loud, earnest, and impossible to mistake for anyone else. He answers Sans's silences by setting another place at the table.

The Repo-Mage of Healthcare — Mages' Guild (Medical Division)

Status: Active — Wandering Raventree Manor demanding co-pays

Parson Pellinost is a 'doctor' for the Mages' Guild who perfectly illustrates the Guild's approach to charity. He bypassed heavy magical wards to enter a barricaded room, healed an injured Archie Miser, informed him he was now in debt, and when Archie demanded a refund, Pellinost forcibly ripped the healing magic back out of Archie's body. Waluigi finds the sheer, unadulterated pettiness of this act to be a breathtaking display of aggressive capitalism. WAH.

Evidence

  • Sabre — “He does not need a sword if the room already contains pain, fear, and someone desperate enough to sign whatever appears in front of them.”
  • Hidden in Plain Sight — “He performs highly effective restorative magic, but his magic comes with an invisible, immediate contract.”
  • Guild Spellcasting — “The Repo-Mage of Healthcare”

description.value: The ghost can see 60 ft. into the Ethereal Plane when it is on the Material Plane, and vice versa.

The ghost can move through other creatures and objects as if they were difficult terrain.

It takes 5 (1d10) force damage if it ends its turn inside an object.

The ghost can move through other creatures and objects as if they were difficult terrain.

Melee Weapon Attack:+5 to hit,, 5 ft., one target. Hit: 17 (4d6 + 3) necrotic damage.

The Ghost attacks with its Withering Touch.

The ghost enters the Ethereal Plane from the Material Plane, or vice versa. It is visible on the Material Plane while it is in the Border Ethereal, and vice versa, yet it can't affect or be affected by anything on the other plane.

Each non-undead creature within 60 ft. of the ghost that can see it must succeed on a DC 13 Wisdom saving throw or be frightened for 1 minute. If the save fails by 5 or more, the target also ages 1d4 x 10 years.

A frightened target can repeat the saving throw at the end of each of its turns, ending the frightened condition on itself on a success. If a target's saving throw is successful or the effect ends for it, the target is immune to this ghost's Horrifying Visage for the next 24 hours. The aging effect can be reversed with a greater restoration spell, but only within 24 hours of it occurring.

Each non-undead creature within 60 ft. of the ghost that can see it must succeed make a Wisdom saving throw. A target can repeat the saving throw at the end of each of its turns, ending the condition on itself on a success.

One humanoid that the ghost can see within 5 ft. of it must succeed on a DC 13 Charisma saving throw or be possessed by the ghost; the ghost then disappears, and the target is incapacitated and loses control of its body. The ghost now controls the body but doesn't deprive the target of awareness.

The ghost can't be targeted by any attack, spell, or other effect, except ones that turn undead, and it retains its alignment, Intelligence, Wisdom, Charisma, and immunity to being charmed and frightened. It otherwise uses the possessed target's statistics, but doesn't gain access to the target's knowledge, class features, or proficiencies.The possession lasts until the body drops to 0 hit points, the ghost ends it as a bonus action, or the ghost is turned or forced out by an effect like the dispel evil and good spell. When the possession ends, the ghost reappears in an unoccupied space within 5 ft. of the body. The target is immune to this ghost's Possession for 24 hours after succeeding on the saving throw or after the possession ends.

One humanoid that the ghost can see within 5 ft. of it must make a Charisma saving throw.

The Competent Royal — Sarasaland / Mushroom Regency Coalition

Status: Active, respected, probably exhausted

Princess Daisy is the ruler of Sarasaland and the person who hosted the Second Diplomatic Summit. She is also, in Waluigi's considered opinion, one of the only royals in the region who actually knows what she's doing. While everyone else was walking out or giving ego-speeches or getting framed for corruption, Daisy managed the chaos, enforced limits, and kept the relief program on track. Waluigi has enormous respect for Daisy because she does the WORK while others take the credit or create the problems. Also, she's one of the few royals who has ever acknowledged Waluigi's existence at social events, which Waluigi appreciates more than he will admit publicly.

The reigning monarch of the Mushroom Kingdom, alive and holding court. Pink gown, golden crown, white gloves, sapphire brooch, parasol. The XP ledger (data/abilityPoints.json) carries her at level 4, so this sheet sits at CR 2: a sovereign, not a duelist.

The present-day record lists her as Deceased — assassinated under circumstances that remain disputed (characters.json princess_peach). Use this sheet for flashback and council scenes only; the present-day portrait portraits/princess_peach.jpg is a different artefact.

description.value: A lace parasol with a steel rib. Finesse; she fights like someone who was taught fencing as a courtesy and took it seriously.

Allies within 30 feet who can see the Princess have advantage on saving throws against being frightened. A hostile creature that can see her must succeed on a DC 15 Wisdom saving throw the first time it tries to attack her on its turn; on a failure it chooses a different target or loses the attack. Creatures immune to being charmed and anyone who has already damaged her are unaffected.
One allied palace guard within 60 feet that can hear her uses its reaction to move up to its speed without provoking opportunity attacks or to make one weapon attack.
While holding the parasol she takes no falling damage, descends at 60 feet per round and can move 2 feet horizontally for every foot she falls. Balconies are exits.

The Ghost Researcher Who Disappeared — Formerly Mushroom Kingdom Royal Science Division / Formerly Boo Research Institute / Formerly Gadd Science Incorporated (dissolved) / Rumored connections to entities Waluigi cannot confirm

Status: Unknown — last confirmed public appearance approximately 1028 BF, current location classified or unknown

Professor Elvin Gadd — known publicly as E. Gadd — was the Mushroom Kingdom's foremost expert on paranormal phenomena, spectral containment, dimensional engineering, and what academic literature delicately calls 'paratechnological development.' He invented the Poltergust, the device Luigi uses to capture ghosts. He invented the Pixelator, a matter-to-data conversion system whose applications remain classified. He invented the Ghost Portrificationizer, the Dark-Light Device, the Dual Scream communicator, and at minimum twenty-three other devices that Waluigi has found references to in fragmentary documentation — most of which are described only by codename and clearance level. He served the Mushroom Kingdom's royal family for over seven decades in various advisory capacities. He trained Luigi personally in ghost-hunting operations. He was present — in some capacity that records do not specify — during multiple events that shaped the kingdom's recent history. And then, approximately twelve years ago, Professor E. Gadd stopped appearing in public. His laboratories were seized by government authority. His research was classified. His name was removed from active academic registries. His former colleagues were discouraged from discussing him. His correspondence was returned unopened. The official explanation is 'retirement to pursue private research.' The unofficial explanation varies depending on who Waluigi asks — some say he discovered something too dangerous to publish, some say he was silenced by parties unknown, some say he simply got tired of institutional politics and walked away. Waluigi has attempted to locate Professor E. Gadd for interview purposes. Waluigi has been unsuccessful. This is unusual, because Waluigi is very good at finding people who do not want to be found. E. Gadd is either dead, dimensionally displaced, or being protected by resources that exceed Waluigi's investigative capabilities. Waluigi does not know which. Waluigi would very much like to find out. WAH.

The Red Scullion's innate spellcasting ability is Charisma (spell save DC 14, +6 to hit with spell attacks). She can innately cast the following spells, requiring no material components:

At will: Detect Magic, Magic Missile

2/day each: Ray of Enfeeblement, Sleep, Bane

1/day: Bestow Curse, Eyebite

For the duration, you sense the presence of magical effects within 30 feet of yourself. If you sense such effects, you can take the Magic action to see a faint aura around any visible creature or object in the area that bears the magic, and if an effect was created by a spell, you learn the spell's school of magic.

The spell is blocked by 1 foot of stone, dirt, or wood; 1 inch of metal; or a thin sheet of lead.

You create three glowing darts of magical force. Each dart strikes a creature of your choice that you can see within range. A dart deals 1d4 + 1 Force damage to its target. The darts all strike simultaneously, and you can direct them to hit one creature or several.

Using a Higher-Level Spell Slot. The spell creates one more dart for each spell slot level above 1.

[[2 + @item.level]]{Level [[lookup @item.level]] darts}

A beam of enervating energy shoots from you toward a creature within range. The target must make a Constitution saving throw. On a successful save, the target has Disadvantage on the next attack roll it makes until the start of your next turn.

On a failed save, the target has Disadvantage on Strength-based D20 Tests for the duration. During that time, it also subtracts 1d8 from all its damage rolls. The target repeats the save at the end of each of its turns, ending the spell on a success.

The hag magically enters the Ethereal Plane from the Material Plane, or vice versa. To do so, the hag must have a heartstone in her possession.

This ugly finger used to belong to a witch or crone but has been turned into a conduit for magical power. It feels cool and clammy in the hand.

A Necromancy spell cast using this wand as the focus can be empowered, but extracts an inescapable cost.

The caster takes damage equal to the spell’s level (1 damage for cantrips) but applies the following effects to the spell:

  • The spell's save DCs increases by 1.

  • The caster can reroll any number of the spell's damage dice once, keeping the second result.

Spellcasting Focus. An arcane focus is a special item designed to channel the power of arcane spells. A sorcerer, warlock, or wizard can use such an item as a spellcasting focus, using it in place of any material component which does not list a cost.

Wondrous item, (requires attunement)

As an action the caster can spend their own life energy to create spell slots. They must expend a number of hit dice equal to double the level of spell slot they want to create, and immediately casts a spell using that slot as part of the action. This can also be used for spells that normally take a bonus action to cast.

Drawback: Using this more than once a day gives a level of exhaustion each time it's used after the first time.

A Koopa with a red armband waved the attackers through the inner gate. Two more were stopped at the edge of the evacuation route: 'You cannot come.' 'Why?' 'You are traitors.
